#2812. Women's rights matter more than any league, say Afghan cricketers

Afghan women's cricketers have accused overseas players signing up for the inaugural Afghanistan Premier League of sending a message to the world that women suffering in the country "can simply be ignored".

Women's participation in sport has been effectively outlawed since the Taliban's return to power in 2021, and many of Afghanistan's female cricketers left the country for their own safety.

The men's franchise league is expected to start in December in the UAE, though it is yet to be sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

In September, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) urged players to reconsider their involvement and batter Ollie Pope withdrew.

"For five years, girls in Afghanistan have been denied the right to play cricket and many other basic rights," Nahida Sapan, who captained the Afghanistan Refugee Women's XI on this summer's tour of England, told the BBC Stumped podcast.

"Foreign players had a real opportunity to stand with millions of Afghan women and girls by choosing not to participate.

"It may have seemed like a small action, but it could have sent a powerful message and put pressure on those responsible.

"This is not about being against cricket or Afghan men's cricket. It is about standing up for basic human rights."

Eight English players were signed in the draft on Tuesday, alongside players from Scotland, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand.

England's Alex Hales, Tymal Mills, Joe Clarke, Olly Stone, Moeen Ali, Luke Wood, Tom Moores and Chris Wood were all signed. Scotland's George Munsey also secured a deal, as did Ireland all-rounder Curtis Campher.

Other England players including Dawid Malan and James Vince also put their names into the draft.

England will have more overseas representation than any other country in the Afghan league.

The major names signed from other nations include Sri Lanka internationals Kusal Perera, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera and Kamindu Mendis, Australian batter D'Arcy Short, South Africa spinner Imran Tahir and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan.

The ECB has refused to schedule bilateral cricket with Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power - a stance Australia also adopts.

England have, however, continued to play against Afghanistan at global events, including World Cups in both limited-overs formats and the Champions Trophy, which resulted in calls from MPs for their game in 2025 to be boycotted.

"For me, the women and girls of Afghanistan come first," said Sapan. "Their rights, dignity and freedom matter more than any league or sporting opportunity.

"Taking part in this league without acknowledging what is happening to Afghan women risks sending the message to the world that their suffering can simply be ignored."

Afghan women ask ICC for 'clear answers' on future

Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule

Afghanistan's women's players have repeatedly called on the ICC to recognise them once again as an international team, and commit to long-term funding.

Without official ICC recognition, they play as the Afghan Refugee Women's Team.

In April 2025, the ICC - together with the cricket boards of England, Australia and India - announced a joint programme to provide financial support for the players, and that funding was extended in July.

"To every international player considering participating in this league, I believe there is a responsibility to ask difficult questions," said batter Firooza Amiri.

"You have the freedom to choose where you play, which organisations you represent and which competitions you participate in, but that freedom also comes with a responsibility to understand the systems you may be helping to support.

"I am not asking international players to turn their backs on the people of Afghanistan. I am asking them to recognise the difference between supporting Afghan people and legitimising a system that has systematically taken away women's rights."

Afghanistan men's team has retained full ICC membership despite the country's inability to meet the membership requirement of supporting a women's national side.

Amiri said their stance was not about withdrawing support for the Afghanistan men's team.

"Imagine your daughter, your sister or your wife being told that she cannot attend school simply because she is a woman," she said. "Imagine being told that she cannot play sport, pursue her ambitions or participate in public life.

"We cannot celebrate the development of cricket in Afghanistan while ignoring the complete exclusion of half of its population from the game.

"The question is whether the international cricket community is prepared to stand by its own values when it comes to Afghan women."

#2811. Trevor Lawrence is having by far the best season of his career

Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman. Instead, Lawrence stayed three years at Clemson and was the first pick in 2021, viewed as a sure-thing quarterback prospect.

In Year 6, Lawrence finally looks like everything he was supposed to be.

Lawrence is having by far the best year of his NFL career, with career-high stats across the board that are constrained only by the fact that the Jaguars win so many blowouts that Lawrence doesn’t throw many passes in the fourth quarter.

So far this season, Lawrence has completed 146 of 224 passes for 1,932 yards, with 18 touchdowns, four interceptions and an NFL-leading passer rating of 111.7. Project Lawrence’s totals to a 17-game season, and he’s on pace to finish with 4,106 yards, 38 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Those are MVP numbers.

Lawrence’s rookie year was a disaster, as he led the league in interceptions while playing on a chaotic Jaguars team coached by Urban Meyer, whose only foray into NFL coaching lasted less than one season. Lawrence and the Jaguars got a lot better once they kicked Meyer to the curb, but even in the next three years with Doug Pederson, an offensive coach with a Super Bowl-winning pedigree, Lawrence didn’t live up to the pre-draft hype.

Playing in Liam Coen’s offense, something has changed. Last year the Jaguars went 13-4, winning double-digit games for the first time since drafting Lawrence, and this year Lawrence and the Jaguars are even better. Lawrence’s average of 8.6 yards per pass is the best of his career by almost a yard and a half, a remarkable improvement for any quarterback to make in his sixth season.

Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on 8 percent of his attempts, the best in the NFL this season and by far the best mark of his career. And after getting sacked a career-high 41 times last year, Lawrence has gotten much more comfortable reading the pass rush in his second year in Coen’s offense and has only been sacked 13 times this season.

Lawrence’s numbers would look even better if the Jaguars weren’t so often taking their foot off the gas late in games because they’re blowing opponents out. Lawrence has 1,196 yards and 12 touchdowns in the first halves of games this season, but he only has 736 yards and six touchdowns in the second halves of games.

The Jaguars currently have the fourth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, and Lawrence has the fifth-best odds to win MVP. That might be underselling them, and him. The Jaguars may just be the best team, with the best quarterback, in the NFL right now.

#2808. Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30

Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference's sole leader.

They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2.

The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse's first as the team's head coach.

Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists.

The Pistons' leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26.

The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons' injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion).

Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks "it'll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is," according to Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit:

Embiid assisted the Sixers' first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown's cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup.

Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer.

The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit's offense grew frigid.

Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes.

Embiid didn't break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He's 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn't made a three since the Sixers' second game.

Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials' review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for "initiating" the altercation.

Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter.

Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers' offense.

Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona's strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch.

Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers' lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn't be surprising at all if Brown's three-point shooting improved from last season's 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers' hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year.

As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage.

The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter.

Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team's lead down to single digits. The Pistons' offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run.

Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers' lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third.

Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers' win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had "neck soreness."

Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory.

Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons' deficit to 106-102.

The Sixers halted the Pistons' run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East's No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

#2807. Ravens doomed by QB injuries, porous defense in loss to Jaguars

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve, the Baltimore Ravens turned to Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

The Ravens scraped their way through a 10-3 first quarter, but the Jaguars literally ran away with the game on a 50-yard Parker Washington touchdown just before halftime. A rainy night in Baltimore contributed to a sloppy second half that, to be frank, could have gotten much worse for the home team. Jacksonville ended up settling for three field goals inside the 30-yard line before another late touchdown – all on short fields – to finish with a 33-10 win.

Fagnano himself was playing with a heavily-bandaged right ankle that clearly limited his dropback capabilities. All of offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's tricks – motion, misdirection, even a healthy dose of Derrick Henry wildcat – could not cover up his quarterback's basic inability to plant on his back foot and drive the ball downfield. The Jaguars rolled out base personnel, loaded the box, and stuffed Henry for just 57 yards on 17 carries. Fagnano completed 10 of his 18 passes – most of them screens and other simple designed throws – for just 60 yards and two interceptions.

The Ravens' struggling offensive operation only compounded the issues. Doyle's trickery made execution even more of a priority for a unit that was playing its first full game with its best starting-five offensive line. But a slew of pre-snap penalties and missed blocks kept the offense behind the sticks and consistently killed their chances to sustain drives. Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford in particular could be seen expressing his frustration at his unit on the sidelines. Outside of a 65-yard garbage-time rushing touchdown from Justice Hill, Baltimore managed just three points and 162 yards on 53 plays (3.05 yards per play).

Defensively, the Ravens picked up where they left off in recent games: on skates. The Jaguars marched down the field with little resistant on their opening drive, going 77 yards in just seven plays before punching in a goal-line touchdown. Baltimore's defense stiffened up after, but Washington's catch-and-run score was exactly the kind of back-breaking coverage collapse that has doomed the unit this year (and for the last few).

It was also exactly the kind of play that would doom a team trying to pull off an upset win with an undrafted rookie under center. A valiant second half – in which the Ravens defense twice forced three-and-out field goals after a Fagnano interception and kept the Jaguars out of the end zone until the game was effectively lost – deserves some mention, but there are no game balls in a defeated locker room. Regardless of the circumstances at quarterback, a team with a defensive-minded head coach; a respected defensive coordinator; an exciting young staff of defensive assistants; and one of the most expensive defensive rosters in football…should be able to play better defense. Standing tall on short fields in the second half means less after giving up a pair of full-length scores that effectively defined the game in the first. All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton also left the game with a hip injury and did not return, raising questions about the status of Baltimore's best defender for Week 10.

A 53-yard field goal from Jake Moody in his Ravens debut was an early highlight for a special teams unit that quickly fell into the same disarray as the team's other two phases. There is almost something impressive about Baltimore's ability to conjure up seemingly-obscure penalties like Rasheen Ali's illegal double-team block on a first-quarter return. And while a fourth-quarter comeback was never realistic, LaJohntay Wester's return fumble still added insult to injury and put an exhausted defense out on the field once again.

With Thursday's loss, the Ravens drop to 4-5, keeping them in last place in the AFC North. They have 10 days ahead of their next game, a Monday night matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. Jacoby Brissett should be in Baltimore by then, assuming Eric DeCosta finalizes the reported trade with the Arizona Cardinals. The 10-year veteran is no doubt an upgrade over Fagnano (not to mention his ankle), but he will face the same adverse circumstances, not to mention the heightened chance for procedural issues with a fourth quarterback under center.

If the Ravens' 2026 season is over, it did not end on a rainy Thursday night in Baltimore. It ended on a sunny afternoon in Buffalo, as soon as Jackson rushed off the field cradling his throwing hand. The loss to the Jaguars represents something different, arguably worse: just how bad things can get.

#2803. LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it

LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top.

In the third quarter of the Sixers' 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he'd take fan interaction to a whole new level.

James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments.

It wasn't until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn't hold back giving reporters a play-by-play.

"I spilled some of his wine," he said postgame. "I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright."

Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN.

"[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said 'My bad,' my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court]."

"At the end of the day he's another man like me," Clemons said. "I mean he's LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it's nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though."

It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans' cups, but it's rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks' court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan's beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate.

If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having.

The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season.

"It's a long marathon. And if you don't find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you're working and even though you're locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us."

Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old's mindset coming into the season.

"This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it's his] 24th year. It's a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he's a big part of that."

The vibes are high. It's difficult for them not to be.

With Monday's win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They've won four in a row and the only team they've lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

#2799. Doc Rivers shares criticisms of Giannis Antetokounmpo's game − and how he can improve

If you ask Doc Rivers, Giannis Antetokounmpo is in the perfect place to take the next step in his career.

In the most recent episode of "The Bill Simmons Podcast," Rivers dished on his time with the Milwaukee Bucks, how he navigated the ill-fated Damian Lillard trade and the highs and lows that came with coaching the Greek Freak.

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers told Simmons. "He's interesting. He's not easy. He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy because he has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way. Downhill. Force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

The number one thing Rivers emphasized was execution. Preparing the right way and setting his teammates up for success is the area the Hall of Fame coach believes Antetokounmpo fell short in during their time together. But now, with Antetokounmpo on the Miami Heat under Erik Spoelstra, Rivers is hopeful that will come to fruition.

"I wish he learned how to execute better," Rivers said. "He's one of those guys − you get a lot of them from the U.S., AAU guys − that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shootarounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach who is as good as there is in execution."

Antetokounmpo landed in South Beach this summer after a blockbuster trade that put an end to the long-running standoff between the 10-time All-Star and the Bucks front office, but it's been anything but greener pastures early on. The Heat are 3-6 in their first nine games despite him averaging 28.3 points and 12.5 rebounds a night.

The Golden State Warriors pulled away from a tie game against Miami at halftime to earn a comfortable 120-100 win Thursday, thanks in no small part to the ability of Draymond Green, Al Horford and Charles Bassey to contain Antetokounmpo to just one point in seven fourth quarter minutes down the stretch.

#2797. Scouting the Enemy: Carolina Panthers

The Denver Broncos will battle Carolina Panthers on Sunday. It's a huge matchup for the Broncos who have a shot to keep their winning streak alive and enter their bye week with a 7-2 record if they are victorious. Here is a deeper look at their Week 9 opponent.

2025 Carolina Panthers Regular Season Review

The Carolina Panthers won the NFC South with an 8-9 record in Head Coach Dave Canales' second season leading the team.. They lost to the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card Round 34-31.

2026 Carolina Panthers Offseason Additions and Departures

After securing their first division title since the 2017 season, the Carolina Panthers made a few big splashes in free agency to be more competitive in 2026. The two high-profile signings came on defense. They signed edge rusher Jaelan Phillips to a four-year, $120 million dollar contract. The Panthers also inked All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd to a three-year, $45 million dollar contract.

Carolina didn't have many big-named departures. However, they parted ways with two starters. Defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson and offensive lineman Austin Corbettt, whose time with the Panthers was marred by injuries.

In the 2026 NFL Draft, they made bolstering their trenches a priority. They took Georgia tackle Monroe Freeling in the first round and Texas Tech defensive tackle Lee Hunter in the second. Both have been starters for them this season. Tennessee wide receiver Chris Brazzell II was their third-round pick. Unfortunately, his rookie season ended early after suffering a torn LCL in summer.

On the bright side, their Day 3 group of talent has earned plenty of playing time. They snagged two starters on Day 3 with Texas A&M cornerback Will Lee and Penn State safety Zakee Wheatley. Fifth-round offensive lineman Sam Hecht and seventh-round linebacker Jackson Kuwatch have earned backup roles and are playing on special teams for them this season.

Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Bryce Young

As noted above, the Panthers made improving their defense a big part of their free agent plans. On offense, they banked on the progression of quarterback Bryce Young to be the catalyst that would take their offense to the next level. He is my X-Factor for them on offense.

It's been an up-and-down season for Young. Even so, the Panthers have had a big turnaround on offense. They are a Top 10 unit in the NFL by most metrics. Wide receivers Tetairoa McMillian and Jalen Coker have been very productive. Tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller have gotten their fair share of looks in the passing game too.

Young has done a great job diving up his targets and despite a less-than-optimal completion percentage. In seven starts, Young is completing 59-percent of his passes, thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions on the season. He is doing great on first down and is moving the chains early and often. However, his third down efficiency has been less than optimal.

A big reason for that is poor play from their offensive line. In just seven games, Young has been sack almost as many times as he was in 2025. This is a game where Denver's defensive front seven needs to make an impact. While their sack total isn't nearly as good as it was last season, they're still a top-ranked team when it comes to generating pressure and getting quarterback hits. If they can rattle Young, I like Denver's odds of winning this game.

Defensive X-Factor: Linebacker Devin Lloyd

The Panthers made some splashes in free agency to upgrade their defense. Alas, it has been their biggest weakness to date. No excuses can be made, but they have had a bunch of injuries. Their poor play and inconsistency led to the firing of Ejiro Evero at the end of October. Broncos Country may remember that name, as Evero was the Defensive Coordinator for the Broncos in 2022 when Nathaniel Hackett was Head Coach.

One bright spot for them on defense has been linebacker Devin Lloyd. He's my X-Factor for them on defense. Lloyd had a Pro-Bowl and All-Pro season in his fourth and final year with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. He notched 135 tackles, 5 interceptions, and 1.5 sacks.

This season, he has continued to play at a high level. The fifth-year pro already has 69 tackles, 2 interceptions, and 2 sacks on the season. If there is any player on defense Denver's offense needs to be cognizant of, it's Lloyd. He has incredible range and playmaking ability. Whether it's against the run or the pass, he is one of the league's most versatile defenders that can make a huge impact on the game.

How the Broncos can achieve a victory over the Panthers

ICYMI: Yesterday, I wrote how the Broncos can achieve their seventh victory of the season over the Panthers. Overall, this is a game where I really like Denver's chances. If they can establish the run on offense and get after Young defensively, they should be able to come away with a big win before the bye week.

Hart's Prediction: Broncos 30, Panthers 17.

#2796. Warriors vs. Heat player grades: Steph Curry explodes as the bench steps up

The Golden State Warriors are officially rolling. With Thursday night's 120-100 win over the Miami Heat, the Dubs have won six games in a row, and their 0-3 start is a distant memory.

Thursday was a game they were expected to win — Miami is off to a sluggish start, and played an overtime game the night before — and win they did, though they once came out of the gates slowly, trailing by 10 early and entering halftime with a tied score. But a win is a win is a win, and a 20-point win is a 20-point win is a 20-point win.

So let's grade the players who got the job done. As always, grades are based on my expectations of each player, with a "B" grade representing the average performance for that player.

Note: True-shooting percentage (TS) is a scoring efficiency metric that accounts for threes and free throws. Entering Thursday's games, league-average TS was 57.1%.

16 minutes, 10 points, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 4-for-6 shooting, 2-for-4 threes, 83.3% TS, -5

Richard got another start, presumably partially due to Gui Santos' absence, and partially due to wanting to get a strong defender on the court against Andrew Wiggins. Richard played awesomely against Wiggins, who shot just 1-for-6 on the day, and also when taking turns on Klay Thompson.

When the Warriors were struggling to start the game, Richard was also the team's lone source of offense … not only was he the first player on the team to reach double digits, but he was the only Dub with double digits at the half.

It's unfair that Richard ended up with a -5 plus/minus on a night where the Warriors won by 20. That's really just the result of him being one of their best players when they were struggling, and then not getting much second-half playing time due to other players heating up. So it goes. They got the win, he played well, and I'm sure he's quite happy with all of it.

Grade: A-Post-game bonus: Worst plus/minus on the team.

30 minutes, 17 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists, 3 steals, 1 block, 2 turnovers, 4 fouls, 6-for-14 shooting, 1-for-3 threes, 4-for-6 free throws, 51.1% TS, -1

Lendeborg — in just the ninth game of his career — has reached the point where you feel like he had a quiet game and then look at the box score and he's sitting on a 17-8-6-3-1 line. Ridiculous!

His NBA crash course continued, as he opened up the game defending Bam Adebayo, and had plenty of possessions against Giannis Antetokounmpo as well. Both of those players had pretty decent numbers, but I was impressed with the job that Lendeborg did when lined up against them.

It wasn't his most efficient shooting night, but we're likely going to see that more and more as he's given a larger and larger role in the offense. Both his efficiency and his plus/minus were hurt by the fact that Steve Kerr trusts Lendeborg to be The Man when Steph Curry and Draymond Green sit … and sometimes when they're on the court, too. As a result, he doesn't always have a ton of help, and there were plenty of shots in this game that he missed because he was the last-second bail-out option. Comes with the territory.

Ultimately, a very strong game for Lendeborg, and one where we really saw him start to further his chemistry with other players on the team, such as Charles Bassey and Brandon Williams.

Grade: B+Post-game bonus: Led the team in rebounds.

27 minutes, 2 points, 5 rebounds, 11 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 3 turnovers, 1 foul, 1-for-3 shooting, 0-for-2 threes, 33.3% TS, +13

Green's patience on offense continues to shine through this year. He's played in seven games this season and only shot the ball 21 times, total. A large part of that is the presence of Lendeborg, who simply makes the offense work much better, and gives the team another 20-point scorer. But part of it is Draymond showing restraint on that end of the court. There will be a time and a place for him to take a lot of shots and score a lot of points, but it is very noticeable how much more fluid the offense is with him acting solely as a facilitator (both with and without the ball).

The season-high 11 assists for Green were a joy to watch, and it was the driving force for the 36 team assists the Dubs had, which was also a season high.

But above all else, this game was a reminder as to the value Green brings on the defensive end, not just through his actions on any given possession, but his abilities that allow Kerr flexibility when game-planning. On paper, Green being the starting center against an opposing frontcourt of Antetkounmpo and Adebayo is a bit silly, but his talent and versatility makes it work.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Led the team in assists.

32 minutes, 9 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 1 turnover, 3 fouls, 3-for-8 shooting, 2-for-6 threes, 1-for-2 free throws, 50.7% TS, +5

It's always a special day when Klay returns to the Bay Area. But when he does, it's hard to ignore the storyline of his departure, even if it's long been buried. A lot went into the Warriors legend deciding to leave the team, but much of it stemmed from being upset at Podziemski starting to take Thompson's spot in the starting lineup, and the way the franchise handled that shift.

While it's easy to understand and empathize with Klay, it's also pretty apparent that the Warriors made the right move. Thompson is headed for the Hall of Fame, but these days Podziemski is certainly the better — and more complete — player.

That was on display Thursday night, even though it wasn't Podz's best game, by the stat sheet or by the eye test. He struggled to get separation against Miami's length, but he played awesome defense and made things happen all over the court.

28 minutes, 29 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists, 1 steal, 1 foul, 9-for-19 shooting, 6-for-12 threes, 5-for-5 free throws, 68.4% TS, +17

Curry was something of a non-factor in the first half. He looked like he simply didn't have it, and shot just 2-for-10 from the field. After the game, Kerr mentioned that one of the most special things about Curry is his ability to bounce back from a bad performance while it's still happening, instead of needing to wait for the next game.

And my goodness was that exemplified in this contest. On the other side of the court was Antetokounmpo, a recent MVP, and Adebayo, who has the second-highest scoring game in NBA history to his name. Yet once the second half began, the contest emphatically belonged to Curry, who was far and away the best player on the court. He truly took over. And thanks to the addition of Lendeborg and the depth of this team, it seems like Curry will be able to do that more and more often this year, given that he doesn't have to expend all his energy carrying the team on his shoulders all the time.

He's still averaging more than a point per minute, and he's under two turnovers per game. The end, I'm pleased to report, is not in sight.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Led the team in points.

18 minutes, 8 points, 5 rebounds, 1 assist, 4 fouls, 3-for-3 shooting, 2-for-2 threes, 133.3% TS, +21

It turns out that having three rest days — Horford didn't play on Monday — is a superpower for Big Al. That probably shouldn't be surprising, considering that this is his 20th NBA season. Against an incredibly athletic team, Horford more than held his own, with elite interior defense and a slick jumper that proved pivotal in the second-half rally.

He remains a savvy and trustworthy veteran on his worst day, and a two-way impact player on his best.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Best plus/minus on the team.

17 minutes, 5 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists, 3 steals, 3 turnovers, 1 foul, 1-for-5 shooting, 0-for-4 threes, 3-for-4 free throws, 37.0% TS, +9

Not the best offensive night for Melton, but it was a fantastic game for him on the other end of the court. His defense has been so strong this year and, just as importantly, his hands have been so active, which helps create healthy chaos. Critically, Melton has been one of — if not the — best player on the team at turning defense into offense this year. It feels like every time he gets a steal he pushes the ball in transition, and every time he gets a deflection, he leaks out for a teammate to find him. The Dubs had 28 points off of turnovers in this game (an 11-point advantage, despite only forcing one more turnover than they committed), and Melton was a big reason why, even if he only put one shot through the hoop.

Great defense, bad offense? We'll call it a wash.

21 minutes, 10 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists, 2 blocks, 2 turnovers, 1 foul, 4-for-7 shooting, 0-for-1 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 63.5% TS, +7

I'm having so much fun watching Williams on the Warriors. He's just such an enjoyable player to watch, and he plays in a way that's been so foreign to the Dubs over the last decade-plus. Good things happen when Williams is on the court, and specifically when he has the ball in his hands. After so much movement of Curry dancing around the perimeter and cutting baseline to baseline, defenses seem completely confused when Williams gets on the court and starts exploding downhill like prime Frank Gore hitting a gap.

He's been a little inconsistent this year in terms of actually finishing, but good things happen regardless, simply by nature of attacking. In this game, however? No problem finishing whatsoever, or dishing to open teammates. He even blocked a pair of shots! A tremendous game for a vital spark plug.

22 minutes, 13 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 5-for-8 shooting, 2-for-5 threes, 1-for-2 free throws, 73.2% TS, +16

Niang is really starting to show up as advertised, and then some. We expected we'd get a heady veteran who made smart plays and drained threes, and that's arriving in spades. What we didn't expect was to get someone who was going to provide such fiery leadership. That was once again on display Thursday, when Niang did something that not many players are willing to do: go nose-to-nose with Bobby Portis Jr.

The forward had a few choice words for Portis while they shoved their foreheads against each other like bucks during mating season. You could see the trash-talking venom in Niang's eyes, and both players were awarded technicals.

It's fight and intensity that the Warriors need, especially with Jimmy Butler III sidelined. And it's also a healthy complement to Green, as Niang is willing to scuffle with anyone — this was his third such instance of the season — but stops short of crossing the line. His teammates really seem to feed off of it.

14 minutes, 8 points, 7 rebounds, 3 blocks, 3 turnovers, 5 fouls, 3-for-4 shooting, 0-for-1 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 82.0% TS, +7.

Fear not, Warriors fans. Kerr has heard your complaints, logged them, and taken action. After this game, Kerr said that Bassey is "earning more minutes for sure," so you can expect him to get larger chunks of minutes going forward.

This wasn't a perfect game from the energetic big. He got a little too careless, which led to three turnovers and five fouls in just 14 minutes. And he lost his perfect shooting night when he hoisted a victory cigar three that badly missed.

But just because he wasn't perfect doesn't mean he wasn't damn good, and Bassey was exactly that: damn good. He's not only figuring out how to finish more effectively, but building up great chemistry with his teammates. His defense is so much better than it was earlier in his career, as he's genuinely turned a liability into an asset, and it comes with a bunch of rebounds, too.

10 minutes, 9 points, 1 steal, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 3-for-3 shooting, 1-for-1 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 116.0% TS, +5

Payton seems healthier this year than he's been in a long time, and it's paying dividends. Kerr has also really figured out a nice role for GPII, who gets to come into the game for a few short bursts and wreak absolute havoc on defense, while cutting to the rim endlessly on offense. The improved depth of the bench has allowed Payton to have a smaller role, and he's positively thriving in it.

Despite it being a 20-point game, there wasn't a lot of garbage time in this game, as the two-way contracts only got one minute and nine seconds of action.

Only one minute of action, but Ike was still able to get in the stat sheet with a board.

Cryer's time is coming. At some point, injury and/or load management will open the door for him to get some consistent run.

Thursday's inactives: Jimmy Butler III, Moses Moody, Kristaps Porziņģis, Gui Santos

#2795. Colchester fans are with us, says boss Cowley

Colchester United manager Danny Cowley says he believes "the supporters are right with us" despite their long winless run.

The U's have not won any of their last 12 matches in all competitions since a 1-0 victory over Rochdale on 29 August.

It is a run of form that has seen Colchester slip to 23rd in League Two ahead of Saturday's FA Cup first round meeting with Worcester City who play in the seventh-tier Southern Football League Premier Division Central

They lost 3-1 to Walsall last Saturday but Cowley told BBC Essex: "We conceded two late goals, but they are still singing our names, they're right behind us."

He said: "Once we got over the initial disappointment of losing, I felt really inspired by the way that they [the fans] stuck with them.

"Maybe it gave us all a lesson, if things haven't gone your way, it's easy to feed your misery... the supporters maybe made me look at myself and all week we've been really positive."

Cowley's side have not reached the second round of the FA Cup since 2021, and were knocked out by MK Dons in round one last season.

"For us the challenge is to still be in the hat come 17:00 on Saturday, still with 99 points to play for in the league," Cowley added.

"If we can achieve that, then it will be a pretty good weekend for us."

#2792. Warriors defense erases Heat big men in second half as Golden State wins 6th in a row

It's hard to know what Steph Curry has been doing during halftime this season. Maybe he's snacking on popcorn. Maybe he's firing himself up by reading internet comments. Maybe Steph is getting pep talks over FaceTime from Natalie Nakase.

Regardless of what he's doing — meditation, yoga, writing letters complaining about affordable housing projects, watching highlights from Season 2 of "Holey Moley" — it's working. Curry shot 4-of-5 from the field, sank three three-pointers, and scored 14 points in the 3rd quarter as the Golden State Warriors outscored the Miami Heat 38-23. The game was tied at halftime, and the Dubs went on to win by 20, with a tidy final score of 120-100.

Curry is now averaging nearly 12 points in third quarters. He's shooting 62.2% from the field and 65% behind the arc and hasn't missed a third-quarter free throw all season. He finished Thursday's game with 29 points, four assists, and six more three-pointers, and has made at least five triples in each of his last four games.

The Warriors won their sixth straight game after starting the season 0-3. They took the victory Thursday night at the expense of two of their old teammates, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson. Wiggins scored just two points, while Captain Klay had 11 points, though he did block two shots. The two former champions combined to shoot 4-for-16 from the field, while Thompson didn't look amused by his Splash Brother clowning around for a photo during the game.

It's tough for those guys, in part because the Heat's warmups for Thursday's game were black shirts with a red flames on the back. It feels like the team let Guy Fieri and the assistant manager of a Hot Topic have final say on the design. It simply doesn't look good for basketball players in their 30's to dress like they're part of a UFC fighter's entourage.

Giannis Antetokounmpo was a constant Warriors trade target before forcing his way to Miami this summer, where it's not going great. He's averaging 28.3 points and 12.5 rebounds but his team is 3-6. Antetokounmpo had 20 points and 14 rebounds in the loss, but most of that production happened in the first half. After halftime, the Greek Freak had four points and four rebounds and took only four shots, clearly frustrated by Draymond Green's defense.

Green scored two points but delivered 11 assists and finished +13 with a steal and a block. Anecdotally, Green's beard also looks darker, which could have been the NBC Sports Bay Area picture quality, but we think it's possible that Draymond is using BED's (Beard Enhancing Drugs).

During one sequence in the second quarter, Green and Curry took turns feeding rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who filled up the box score with 17 points, eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, and a block.

Lendeborg was part of a high-effort rebounding performance by the Warriors, who grabbed 44 boards to Miami's 39, even with the massive Anteotkounmpo and Bam Adebayo (18 points, 10 rebounds) manning the middle. The bench made a big difference, collecting 24 boards while the Heat's reserves got seven. Standouts were Charles Bassey, De'Anthony Melton, and Al Horford, who had seven, six, and five rebounds respectively. Bassey and Horford each scored eight points and Horford was +21, making both his threes and has five in his last two games.

Bassey played 14 "loud minutes," according to Bob Fitzgerald, and it's hard to argue with that description. He simply does a lot of stuff, even if some of that is negative (five fouls, three turnovers, airballed a three). Bassey blocked three shots and appeared to make the Heat big men decidedly uncomfortable. His most impressive play came when he grabbed a free throw rebound while getting double teamed and fouled, and flipped in a shot anyway.

Once again, the Warriors started slow and fell behind by double-digits early, mainly because they started with ice-cold shooting. The young guys kept the team afloat as the veterans slowly loosened up, with Will Richard leading the team with 10 first-half points and Yaxel adding nine.

The Warriors bench shot 19-for-30, while their Heat counterparts were 8-for-27. Nikola Jovic's long-term deal already looks regrettable. Bobby Portis tried to fire up his team by going after Georges "The Minivan" Niang, and after Niang didn't back down, Portis didn't score for the rest of the game. Niang was 4-for-5 with 10 points after halftime.

Miami sacrificed a ton of their depth to land the Greek Freak, and as a result, only Pelle Larsson is truly reliable off the bench. They're leaning on guys on the downside of their careers, like Thompson and Tim Hardaway, Jr., along with guys taken off the NBA scrap heap, like center Nick Richards. And that could have been the Warriors!

It's never been clear how realistic the Warriors' reported pursuit of Antetokounmpo was at last year's deadline, and they appeared to be a non-factor in the summer's trade talks. The Milwaukee Bucks may not have seriously wanted anyone aside from Brandin Podziemski, and if they weren't going to take Jimmy Butler back, the only way Golden State could have landed Antetokounmpo was too gut their roster and fill in the gaps with, well, guys who didn't have a lot of other options.

They also wouldn't have Yaxel, who is already better than anyone on the Heat besides Bam and Giannis. The Curry Flurry was the engine behind the team's second-half surge, but the team made their game-defining 17-3 run in the quarter by playing defense best described as "really annoying" — something that the Heat used to specialize in. Richard, Melton, Podziemski, and Lendeborg all deflected passes and closed out on threes, causing a number of low-percentage shots late in the shot clock.

Big Al had an embarrassing play where Adebayo faked him out and hit a stepback jumper in the second quarter as Horford stumbled backwards. However, in the remaining 28 minutes following that play, Horford only scored one fewer point than the 83-point man.

The game could have become a true blowout were it not for Davion Mitchell going off in the final quarter, scoring 16 points on 7-for-11 shooting and proving beyond a doubt that there's no better NBA career move than leaving the Sacramento Kings.

Brandon Williams had another solid bench effort with 10 points, four assists, and two surprising blocks. He continued to get to the rim at will off the dribble, getting layups and drawing fouls. Williams' defense has been far better than advertised, and down the stretch, he iced the game by repeatedly finding his teammates for alley-oops.

Why does Williams need to seize this opportunity so badly? He's gotta pay rent in San Francisco.

Let's just say we wouldn't be shocked if Williams is really invested in NBA Cup games and the massive payouts that go to winners. If he can secure one of the six-figure playoff shares, maybe he won't have to get extra roommates from Craigslist.

The Warriors have two more games left on this extended homestand. They'll face the Orlando Magic, missing Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs, on Saturday, then the red-hot New Orleans Pelicans Monday, who will be on a back-to-back, to the Warriors' advantage. Also to the Warriors' advantage? They're the Pelicans.

Six wins in a row, with an excellent chance to stretch their winning streak to eight games before a brutal trip to the Texas Triangle next week. Imagine how good they could be if the first few minutes of the game didn't stink!

#2790. Luka Garza is making life easier for the Celtics

Hours before the Boston Celtics and Milwaukee Bucks faced off Wednesday night, Luka Garza was already getting to work. He joined the team's Stay Ready crew, warming up alongside Mitchell Robinson and Jordan Walsh while his father, Frank, watched from courtside near the baseline.

Garza wasn't in Boston's Jayson Tatum-less starting lineup, but that didn't matter. His routine remained the same.

That's standard for Garza. Each night, he knows the moment could arrive when Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla calls his number. On Wednesday, it came early, with 5:37 remaining in the first quarter. He checked in for Hugo González and knocked down his first shot — a wide-open 3-pointer from the wing — to extend Boston's lead over Milwaukee to 25-8.

Down the other end, less than a minute later, Garza came away with a steal. Payton Pritchard capitalized on the extra possession by draining a jumper. Garza knocked down each of his three 3-point attempts to lead the Celtics with 11 points at halftime. Mazzulla didn't turn to him nearly as much in the second half, but he had already made his impact felt.

In just 18 minutes against Milwaukee, Garza reinforced his reliability.

Oct 14, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Boston Celtics center Luka Garza (52) shoots the ball during warmups prior to a game against the Charlotte Hornets at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

He went from playing 8.9 minutes per game through the first five games of the season to averaging 18.7 over the last three against Orlando, Houston and Milwaukee. In return, Garza has rewarded Mazzulla's increased deployment of the 27-year-old veteran, posting averages of 12.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, and two assists since the start of November.

Throughout it all, Garza has maintained his knack for creating second chances on the offensive glass. He's grabbed 15 offensive rebounds, just behind Robinson (17) and Neemias Queta (18) for the team lead. He's also re-emerged as a dangerous 3-point threat, much like last season. His 52.4% clip from beyond the arc leads the Celtics and ranks first among Eastern Conference centers averaging at least 2.6 attempts.

From the corners, Garza has shot 6-of-8, going 11-of-21 overall from three through the first eight games this season.

The drive-and-kick option for teammates like Paul George and Pritchard to find Garza on the perimeter was utilized Wednesday night, and it's proven to be an effective one. Garza is Mazzulla's best 3-point shooter among Boston's centers, making him a legitimate outside shooting threat that opposing defenses can't afford to leave unattended.

Entering a season where Queta vs. Robinson starting center debates dominated the discourse surrounding Boston's front court, Garza has quietly made his case to play each night. He's done his part to support the group amid Robinson's early-season adjustment struggles by remaining prepared to contribute. And despite understanding what playing behind Queta and Robinson could mean for his minutes on any given night, Garza has emerged as a leader by example in Boston's reserve unit.

The Celtics can call on him to perform alongside the starters while also counting on him to work with those coming off the bench. Garza occupies something of an older brother role in helping teammates navigate the same challenges he previously faced during his three-year stint with the Minnesota Timberwolves.

In Boston, he's able to simultaneously shine and stay hungry.

It doesn't take much for Garza to make a difference either. Sometimes it'll go unnoticed when he battles for a second-chance opportunity because the Celtics fail to convert. Other times, he might not get the seven 3-point attempts he did in Houston. But the effort is always there.

This season, he's averaging 7.5 points with 3.1 rebounds on 48.7 percent shooting. That doesn't even begin to tell half the story of what he's been doing on the floor.

The Celtics can't offer Garza 60-plus starts, but the coaching staff remains vigilant at all times. His impact off the bench has been rewarded, sending the message that the team is well aware of what he's brought to the table. #2786. Haaland has the final say as Manchester City survive Leipzig fightback

Looking to extend their unbeaten home run, RB Leipzig welcomed Manchester City to Saxony for the fourth outing of their Champions League campaign.

Meanwhile, City, still engulfed in legal trouble, arrived hoping to return to winning ways after back-to-back Premier League defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton.

It was the hosts who made the livelier start, with Antonio Nusa providing the first meaningful effort of the encounter in the 15th minute. Cutting in from the right, the Norwegian unleashed a powerful strike from the edge of the box, though Gianluigi Donnarumma remained unfazed as the ball flew straight at him.

From there, Leipzig took control, with Nusa at the heart of proceedings as Martín Demichelis' side pinned City inside their own half for the best part of 15 minutes.

Christoph Baumgartner, Brajan Gruda and David Raum all tried their luck, while City had to wait until the 36th minute for their first effort since the early stages, with Phil Foden digging out a shot from the edge of the box following a wonderful first touch.

Yet, a matter of seconds later, Manchester City took the lead completely against the run of play.

Latching onto a long ball to the left, Nico O'Reilly sent the ball back across the box, where it failed to find a teammate. Instead, it reached the unfortunate Castello Lukeba, whose momentum left him helpless as he prodded the ball beyond Maarten Vandevoordt and into his own net.

The visitors may have edged the possession statistics, but it was Leipzig who had every reason to feel hard done by as the half-time whistle sounded.

In years gone by, this would be the point where we wax lyrical about a Manchester City side who overcame a difficult start to produce one of those marvellous midweek performances that so many across the continent have fallen victim to.

Leipzig know that feeling better than most, having conceded 22 goals in seven meetings with the 2023 European champions. This time, however, the Red Bulls had other ideas.

Demichelis' side came flying out of the blocks after the restart, with Baumgartner once again lifting the crowd with an ambitious effort from distance.

The early pressure was soon rewarded, as Leipzig found themselves level less than three minutes into the second half.

Having fallen behind in such unfortunate circumstances, there was perhaps a touch of justice in the manner of their equaliser, as Ridle Baku's attempted low cross somehow found its way into the bottom corner, catching Donnarumma off his line as the Italian anticipated a delivery into the middle.

Gruda, whose late winner against PSV had already made him a Champions League hero in his debut campaign, was pulling the strings down the right, while Demichelis turned to Christopher Nkunku from the bench, a player with a hattrick to his name against City in 2022.

Yet, for all their control, Leipzig once again found themselves staring at a deficit.

City had barely threatened since the restart, but in the 58th minute, Iliman Ndiaye delivered a wonderful ball for Enzo Fernández, who powered home to restore the visitors' advantage.

For the second time, Leipzig had been punished despite looking the better side. And for the second time, they had an answer, though their first deficit had lasted just under 10 minutes of playing time. This time around, they needed only three.

Gruda combined with Ezechiel Banzuzi on the edge of the area before substitute Nkunku picked out Nusa, who drilled an emphatic finish into the net from the left side of the box.

Having tormented City's defence from the opening exchanges, the Norwegian finally had the goal his performance deserved.

Leipzig were level again at 2-2, and City, for all their experience on the European stage, were finding this particular trip to Saxony anything but straightforward.

But for all their efforts, Leipzig found themselves undone once again, as Erling Haaland slid home to restore City's lead with just over 10 minutes remaining.

The Norwegian had been unusually quiet on the night, but if there is one lesson to be learned from City's aforementioned European exploits, it is that their towering frontman can never truly be written off.

Elliot Anderson, who had tried his luck only moments earlier, powered down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball towards the back post, where Haaland slid in to guide it into a virtually empty net for his fifth in three Champions League outings this season.

Leipzig skipper Raum and City midfielder Rayan Cherki both rattled the crossbar as the chances began to flow in the final quarter of an hour, and the hosts were not out of the clash just yet.

Four minutes of additional time were signalled, and Leipzig were handed one final opportunity when substitute Allan needlessly conceded a free-kick out on the left. But despite teasing deliveries from Raum and Gruda, City stood firm, before Jeremy Doku lifted an effort over the bar at the other end.

In the end, this was hardly a vintage Manchester City performance on the European stage. For long spells, Leipzig had been the better side, and twice they had fought their way back into the contest.

Yet, as has so often been the case on the continent, City found a way to win, condemning Demichelis to his first home defeat in charge of the club.

#2783. 6 cooked NBA teams already serving up a lost season

The NBA's 82-game regular season leaves plenty of margin for error for a bad stretch of play. This is a league where 53% of teams make the playoffs, not counting the four other teams who have the opportunity to earn their way into the postseason with one or two wins in the play-in tournament. There are still five months left on the schedule, with back-to-backs and spells of three-games-in-four-nights filling in the calendar.

Most teams can get off to a bad start and still be just fine. Some teams already know their season is over before it ever really starts. Check out our NBA power rankings this week for full coverage of the league.

Just over two weeks into the season, it already feels like there are six teams who are already toast. Some of these teams knew they would be bad coming into the year, while others dreamed of breaking into the playoffs. The unfortunate reality for these teams is they can't even count on a high draft pick next year anymore after the league's anti-tanking lottery reform was put in place this season ahead of the 2027 draft. Of course, there's plenty of time for things to change with only about 10% of the schedule complete, but these six teams already look cooked.

The Kings appeared to have no hope coming into the season, and at this point the only intrigue left is to see if they avoid being the worst team of the 2020s, a stake currently held by the 14-win Detroit Pistons in 2023-24. Rookie guard Darius Acuff is the best thing this franchise has going for them, and he's getting thrown into the deep end from the very start of his career. Acuff leads the NBA in minutes per game and he's one field goal attempt behind 2-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the league-lead in that category. The Kings could probably stand to give some of Acuff's usage (32.5%) to Domantas Sabonis (16.1% usage rate), but they would still be a bad team, and at least now the rookie guard has the ability to learn from his mistakes. Keegan Murray being out again with an ankle injury after only playing 23 games last year is the real bummer for the start of this season. The Kings felt like the worst team in the league entering the season, and they still feel like the worst team in the league. Try to enjoy the Acuff roller coaster, Kings fans, because there's nothing else to latch onto.

The good news is that rookie forward Caleb Wilson looks like he can be the franchise player the Bulls have been missing since their horrible Jimmy Butler trade 10 years ago. The bad news is they might need four new starters around him long-term. It's been a truly disappointing start for Matas Buzelis, who looked like a keeper in his first two seasons under Billy Donovan, but is regressing and seemingly falling out of favor under new head coach Tiago Splitter. Buzelis' inability to beat mismatches when teams put their tiny guards on him is the single most alarming trend of this season for Chicago. Josh Giddey has also been terrible, and likely won't be around the next time the Bulls have a playoff team. No. 15 overall pick Dailyn Swain can't even get on the floor during blowouts. Chicago's perimeter defense is atrocious with Giddey and Norm Powell, it can't grab a defensive rebound (No. 28 in d-rebound rate), and it's dead-last in three-point percentage. This team stinks out loud, but a brutal schedule to open the season will get softer eventually, and Wilson's highlights will at least give the fanbase something to dream on.

It was simply unavoidable that the Bucks would be in for a hard season after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo, and it's playing out as expected. Milwaukee is hanging tough in most of their games under new head coach Taylor Jenkins, but they just don't have the talent to win in the fourth quarter yet. Milwaukee is dead-last at forcing turnovers on defense, and they're near the bottom of the league in both free throw rate and free throw percentage. The Bucks just don't get anything easy right now, which is the true sign of a terrible team. There are some positives thus far: rookie guard Brayden Burries looks pretty good despite a cold start as a shooter, while Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Tyler Herro are both playing well enough to fetch something decent on the trade market. Kel'el Ware, who is playing under 19 minutes per game, has possibly been the biggest disappointment here so far with a lot of sloppy turnovers, undisciplined fouls, and bricked jumpers to start the year. Getting Ware going next to Burries would at least improve the vibes the rest of the way.

The Suns became the feel-good story of last season by grinding out 45 wins with maximum effort on the offensive glass and forcing defensive takeaways. This year's team had to take a step forward after trading their last remaining future first-round pick for Miles Bridges, but it was easy to tell that move was doomed to fail from the start. Bridges hasn't added much of anything to Phoenix at either end of the floor, but that's just the start of their problems. This team continues to play Jalen Green over Collin Gillespie for some reason, even though every piece of evidence points to Gillespie being the exact player they need. The Suns have more of a chance to turn it around this season than most of these other teams provided they finally start playing their best point guard, but their issues in the middle don't have such an easy solution. I loved Khaman Maluach as a draft prospect, but he just doesn't look ready for starting center minutes at all right now. Oso Ighodaro has been better offensively, but he's too small to play full-time center, and the defense completely falls apart when he's on the floor (a ghastly 129 defensive rating in his minutes). Devin Booker is getting paid enough to lift this team through tough times, but he's just not a great enough shot-maker to overcome his lack of rim attempts. Phoenix has some chance to turn it around, but the early returns are highly discouraging.

I was foolish enough to think the Jazz could be a playoff team this year, but my optimism started to fade once Jusuf Nurkic went down with a foot injury in the team's preseason opener. A length injury to Jaren Jackson Jr. followed, which has put an already thin front court in a dangerous spot to start the season. It's a bad sign that Utah's offense has been the main culprit for their struggles, ranking No. 29 in the league right now. There should be a ton of firepower here, but the team has been ice cold from three (31.5 percent, No. 27 in the league), and rookie Darryn Peterson is still figuring out his spots on the floor. Peterson is relying way too heavily on floaters and other non-rim two-pointers right now, and it's tanking his efficiency (46.5% true shooting). There's also just a huge lack of high-level passing on this team right now, and it's one reason why Lauri Markkanen just can't seem to get going. The JJJ trade looks like an abomination. This was supposed to be the season the Jazz finally stopped rebuilding and started getting serious, but the product on the floor remains extremely poor.

The Clippers' future was decimated by the NBA for their dealings with Kawhi Leonard in a cap circumvention scandal, but they still had a chance to be competitive this year. It already feels like that hope is over. Brandon Ingram reported to training camp with a partially torn Achilles, Max Strus is just returning now from a foot injury, and the big man room might be the worst in the league. Meanwhile, Darius Garland is turning the ball over like crazy, and rookie Keaton Wagler might be the worst inside the arc scorer in the NBA (25% on two-pointers). The Clippers turn the ball over more than any team in the league, and only four clubs allow their opponents to score with better efficiency. Worst of all, they owe their 2027 draft pick to the Thunder. I have mad respect for Ty Lue as a head coach, but there's nothing he can do to stop this mess.

#2781. Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins preview, prediction: On Paper

The Detroit Lions are beat up after a physical and emotional win over the Minnesota Vikings. And while they must travel to play a 1-6 Miami Dolphins team, they can't afford to underestimate them. The NFC North is too competitive for a trap game, and the Dolphins are a little scrappier than they appear.

But is there a real chance of an upset in Miami, or are the Lions clearly the better team? Let's examine it in our Lions vs. Dolphins preview and prediction. It's time for On Paper.

The Lions' passing offense remains one of their most reliable units on the team. While last week's performance against the Vikings wasn't explosive, it was certainly a lot better than most teams manage against Minnesota's defense. While the DVOA ranking remains outside the top five, I still believe Detroit's passing attack should be in that top tier.

Detroit is humming in all facets of their passing attack. In pass protection, the Lions allow the fifth-lowest pressure percentage (30.1%), rank seventh in pass-block win rate (54%), and rank third in PFF team pass-blocking grade (75.1).

The Dolphins may have a worse pass defense than the Lions. Five out of the seven quarterbacks who have faced Miami have finished with a passer rating of 119.8 or higher. Granted, they've played some really good quarterbacks in Brock Purdy, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Still, those quarterbacks have outperformed their year-long efficiency against Miami, and the DVOA ranking—which adjusts to opponents' strength—proves this is a bad pass defense.

This is the result of having an extremely young and inexperienced back seven.

Though there is some recent hope for Miami's pass rush. As Erik Schlitt pointed out in his Honolulu Blueprint, while the season-long stats don't look great for the Dolphins' ability to get to the passer (35.6% pressure rate, 18th; 4.2% sack rate, 28th), they've started to put things together. All nine of their sacks have come in the last four games, and they've posted a pressure rate of 39.5% or higher in three out of four of those games (league average is around 36%).

Over those last four games, the Dolphins' pass defense has been better, but certainly not good. From Weeks 4-8, Miami ranks 27th in dropback EPA (0.180) and 29th in success rate (50.7%).

Player to watch: Sam LaPorta. It's been a quiet few weeks for the Lions tight end, but Miami is allowing the sixth-highest yardage to tight ends (483 yards) and tied for the fourth-most touchdowns (six).

Advantage: Lions +3. This is a top-five unit vs. a bottom-five unit. The only reason I'm not giving it a higher advantage is that some things are trending Miami's way, and weather could also play a factor, with some slight chance of rain.

The Lions' rushing attack still has frustrating bouts of inconsistency, but last week's performance against the Vikings felt like a revelation. Whether Detroit's sidecar formation was a Vikings-specific answer or the cracking of the code for the entire season, we'll see. But it shows one thing for certain: Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing is capable of finding some answers.

For the season, the Lions rushing attack now ranks:

But I must continue to repeat myself that the negative plays are a big problem. The Lions' 19.3% stuffed rate is sixth in the NFL. Those figures are down from last week (20.9%, third-highest), but it still remains an issue to track. Detroit's power success rank also improved after last week, but they still rank just 24th, converting on just 59% of short-yardage situations.

Still, it's worth pointing out how both the offensive line and the running backs are doing their parts. Detroit's line ranks third in adjusted line yards, eighth in run block win rate, and fourth in PFF run blocking grade. Meanwhile, Detroit's backfield ranks sixth in rushing yards over expected per rush (+0.5), sixth in yards after contact per rush (3.38), and Jahmyr Gibbs ranks fourth in missed tackle forced rate (31.9%).

This chart doesn't exactly vibe with the Dolphins' bottom-10 DVOA ranking. They're not giving up a ton of yards nor a ton of yards per carry. So what gives? Let's look deeper.

In short, it appears the Dolphins don't give up a ton of big, explosive plays, but they essentially give up exactly what the offense needs. That's backed by data. Miami has only given up 21 rushes of 10+ yards (t-14th), and just three rushes of 20+ yards (t-sixth fewest).

The good news is the Dolphins are weak where the Lions' run offense struggles. They've produced just a 14.9% stuffed rate (23rd), and they rank 21st in power success rate, allowing conversions on 68% of short-yardage situations.

Player to watch: Jacob Rodriguez. The Dolphins rookie linebacker has been a fun player to watch thus far. Rodriguez has been credited with 30 "stops" per PFF (plays that are a failure for offense), which is second most among ALL NFL linebackers, not just rookies. Seventeen of those have come in the run, t-eighth most.

Advantage: Lions +1.5. I'm not sure I'd expect a huge game from Gibbs and company, given that Miami has not allowed over 150 rushing yards in a game. But Detroit should be fairly efficient on the ground.

It hasn't been a great start to the year for Malik Willis in his new home, but it's hard to blame him given the supporting cast. He's got an extremely young receiving corps, a new offensive system, and an imbalanced offensive line. As a result, the Dolphins rank:

The Dolphins aren't a complete disaster, but they're clearly below average.

That said, there are some very interesting advanced statistics surrounding Willis. For one, he's not afraid to chuck it deep. He currently owns the third-highest average depth of target (9.2), and his deep ball percentage of 16.4% ranks first in the NFL (yes, above Jordan Love, too). But he also ranks third in time to throw (3.05), suggesting he likely holds onto the ball too long—especially when you consider the Dolphins have the second-highest sack rate (10.3%).

The offensive line is a mixed bag. Though they've allowed the second-highest pressure rate (43.2%), they rank 20th in pass block win rate and 31st in PFF pass blocking grade. The issue is that the left side of their offensive line is good-to-great (LT Patrick Paul is 14th in pass blocking grade, rookie LG Kadyn Proctor is improving) and the right side is a disaster (RT Austin Jackson is dead last in pass blocking grade, RG Jonah Savaiinaea is 63rd out of 76).

And as mentioned before, the receiving corps is ridiculously young: Malik Washington is 25; Caleb Douglas is 23, and Chris Bell is 22. Young doesn't mean bad, but it'll take them some time to get adjusted to the NFL.

Is the Lions' pass defense actually getting better? It's hard for me to tell. The raw numbers are improving, but as the chart above shows, they've also played some pretty bad passing offenses in the last few weeks. I'm not yet convinced.

I think it's also worth noting that the Lions' pass rush has fallen off a bit as of late. After three weeks, the Lions ranked 10th in pressure rate (39.0%) and second in time to pressure (2.46). The Lions now rank just 17th in pressure rate (35.8%) and 20th in time to pressure (2.68). And this week, they're almost certainly without DJ Wonnum, who was fourth on the team in pressures (14). That said, the Lions still do rank third in pass rush win rate, third in PFF pass rush grade, and seventh in sack rate. I just worry it's trending in the wrong direction.

Then, of course, there are the injuries to account for. While it looks like Brian Branch is on track to play, the Lions don't have MIKE linebacker Jack Campbell, and top cornerback D.J. Reed is trending toward missing this game. Detroit's back seven has already struggled immensely in coverage, and now they'll be tested further.

Player to watch: Malik Washington. Washington leads the Dolphins in catches (31) and yards (329), and the Dolphins like to use him all over the field—as a screen weapon or downfield. His 4.47 speed is a weapon.

Advantage: Draw. I'm not particularly impressed with either unit. I think it's certainly possible Willis hits on a few big downfield plays, and I think it's also very possible Detroit is able to disrupt and sack Willis 4-6 times this game. In the end, I think it'll all even out.

This is another weird statistical oddity for Miami. By the charts, it looks like they actually have a good thing going with their run game, including a breakout season from Ollie Gordon (408 yards, 4.5 YPC, 4 TDs) and some quarterback rushing potential from Malik Willis (225 yards, 3 TDs). Yet, the advanced statistics aren't as impressive. They rank:

It turns out this rushing attack is very boom or bust—like a less-efficient version of Detroit's running game. They have produced t-sixth-most rushes of 10+ yards (26), but also a 19.1% stuff rate—seventh-highest.

The problem appears to be that the offensive line isn't carrying their end of the bargain. They rank 26th in run block win rate, 27th in PFF run blocking grade, and 27th in adjusted line yards.

But credit to Gordon for doing everything he can to get the most out of his situation.

I don't know, man. The Lions are just too inconsistent in the run game this year. They've been better lately, but it seems like they're still susceptible to explosive plays. Overall, the Lions rank:

So that pretty much matches my eye test. They're decent down-to-down, but they give up too many explosives. Though they've only allowed 21 rushes of 10+ yards (t-14th fewest), they've allowed six of 20+ yards (t-ninth most).

And with the loss of Jack Campbell, it's hard to know how this unit will respond. Detroit has an experienced linebacking corps in Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske, but none provide the instincts and consistency of Campbell.

Player to watch: Tyleik Williams. I pointed it out in my Dolphins vs. Patriots thoughts, but Miami really struggled against New England's nose tackle last week, and Williams remains an impossible guy to move.

Advantage: Dolphins +1. I'm giving Miami a slight advantage here for a couple of reasons. First, I am concerned about the loss of Jack Campbell, and it may take a couple of weeks for Detroit to find a plan that works without him. Second, I do think Willis provides a legitimate rushing threat, and Detroit has lost contain far too often this year. Third, I just think Miami is better than their stats suggest, and the Lions may be a tad worse. It shouldn't be a dominant day for Miami—and if Detroit can get out to a big lead, they can erase this advantage completely—but I still think Miami has the slight edge here.

On Paper drops to 5-2 overall and 3-4 against the spread, but I don't feel all that bad for how my Lions vs. Vikings preview played out. The only area I made a clear mistake was underestimating the Lions' run game, and for the first half of that game, I looked right. But Petzing made a lot of believers on Sunday, and I'm one of them.

In the comment section, we nearly had two perfect predictions, despite the odd score. Muddy.D's 19-16 Lions prediction was just a single point away, as was Devil Barrel's 18-15 Lions prediction. Here is your prize. Share it, or I'll take it back, and you get nothing.

It's a football lasso. Just in case you happen to commit the awful sin of spinning a football near an opponent, you can rope it back in before any ref sees!

The Lions come out with a pretty definitive +3.5 advantage. I know the Dolphins have kept it close with some recent opponents, but I'm not really buying it. There isn't a single thing they do particularly well, and their worst unit (pass defense) happens to match up with Detroit's best unit (pass offense). I think that could spell disaster for Miami, as they don't want Malik Willis dropping back 50 times to try and keep pace with Jared Goff.

I think we get our first comfortable Lions win since the Cardinals game. Lions 38, Cardinals 24.
