#2780. Talking points as Premiership prepares for international break

The Scottish Premiership resumes for one more round of fixtures before this month's international break.

Six games, five kick-off times, lots of issues to address.

Last weekend turned out to be a good one for Rangers in more ways than one.

A late Ryan Naderi goal sealed a Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen on Saturday evening.

And, on Sunday at lunchtime, Premiership leaders Celtic lost in Falkirk, opening up the possibility of Rangers reducing the gap at the top to a point before the reigning champions host Kilmarnock on Sunday.

However, to do that, Derek McInnes' side, now unbeaten in 11 outings, must win away to St Mirren on Saturday.

The last time Rangers were in the Saturday 20:00 slot, they dropped two points away to Dundee and another warning for the Ibrox side is St Mirren's recent home form - a draw with Hibernian and a victory over in-form Dundee.

Craig McLeish's side havw won just once in eight games but ran Rangers pretty close the last time the sides met in Glasgow, only a late Bojan Miovski goal separating the sides.

The Buddies are holding their own in the Premiership this term, sitting eighth within touching distance of the top six at this early stage and St Mirren led Celtic in a Saturday night contest before eventually losing 2-1 in early September.

An intriguing match under the lights awaits.

Hibs were the other League Cup semi-final victors, coming from a goal down to beat Edinburgh rivals Heart of Midlothian 2-1 to end a seven-game run without a win.

The task for Marink Reedijk and his side now is to get their Premiership form in order before returning to Hampden to face Rangers in mid-December.

Under their new Duthc coach, Hibs have taken only one point from a possible 12 so far and prop up the table having played 11 games.

Aberdeen host the Edinburgh side on Saturday evening and the Dons themselves need a turnaround in fortunes in the league, having lost two in a row in the division prior to their semi-final defeat by Rangers.

Stephen Robinson's side are third from bottom, three points better off than Hibs, and the sides drew 1-1 at Easter Road only last month.

It's perhaps still a tad early to be talking in terms of crisis for either club, particularly given Hibs could end the calendar year with a trophy in the cabinet, but both teams need to get a bit of a move on to preserve their top-six ambitions.

Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?

Late Duran double downs Besiktas to give Celtic first Europa League win

Injury-hit and error-ridden Hearts slump to defeat in Thun

Last week's Saturday results in the Premiership did little to break up the clutch of clubs jostling for position in the middle of the table.

It could be a similar story this weekend with Dundee United hosting Motherwell and a Tayside derby between St Johnstone and Dundee, with both at 15:00 GMT on Saturday.

Well ended their long wait for a win by beating St Mirren at home last weekend while St Johnstone twice fought back with 10 players to draw 2-2 with Kilmarnock as the Dundee duo had the weekend off.

Motherwell's 3-0 win over United in early September is their biggest of the league season so far, the visitors having played most of that match with 10 men.

The same day, Dundee thought they were on their way to three points when they led late on against Saints at Dens, but the Perth side had other ideas with an even later equaliser.

With Dundee one point behind Falkirk and United one point further back, both have the chance to move above the Bairns before they face Hearts on Sunday.

Celtic bounced back from defeat by Falkirk with a stirring 3-2 victory at home to Besiktas in the Europa League.

Earlier on Thursday, injury ravaged Hearts lost 3-1 to Thun in Switzerland.

As such, both Scottish sides play their Premiership fixtures on Sunday.

Rangers' result the night before will either offer encouragement or added pressure, with leaders Celtic four points clear of Rangers and the same margin of points between second place and Hearts as things stand.

With one win now in seven games and with 10 first-team players missing on Thursday, Wouter Vrancken and his squad are desperate for the respite provided by the international break.

First, though, the must host in-form Falkirk, who are bidding for five wins in a row. The Bairns' first league win of the campaign was at home to Hearts back in mid-September. They have seldom looked back.

By half-time at Tynecastle, Celtic will be getting ready to kick off against Kilmarnock. Misfiring Kasper Hogh's only three Celtic goals so far came in a 5-1 win at Rugby Park back in August.

Fellow summer signing Camilo Duran has done most of the scoring for Celtic since, including a double (a Duran Duran if you will) against Besiktas.

Whoever starts in attack for the hosts, second-bottom Killie will have their work cut out to improve a run of one win in six outings.

#2779. An All-22 look inside the blitzing arsenal of Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores

A game against the Vikings means your offense will get the full Brian Flores Experience, a blitz-crazed defense that sends two or three extra rushers at your offensive line…all game.

That's what the Buffalo Bills have in front of them on Monday Night Football in Week 9. Entering this contest, Minnesota owns the league's highest blitz rate (on dropbacks) at 74.2%. The Commanders are second at 44.5%, and the league average is 31.2%. Minnesota blitzes frequently on run plays too.

Let's dig into the ingenuity of Flores' enormous blitzing arsenal.

We'll begin in Week 1, Minnesota's game against Jordan Love and the Packers.

What you'll see below is Vikings in an overload look to the left side of the Packers offensive front… with four defenders on the line of scrimmage on that side of the ball, compared to just two on the other side of the center.

But at the snap is when the calculated chaos ensued.

Cornerback Byron Murphy, who initially looked to be covering Christian Watson in a tight split near the numbers on the upper portion of the screen, screamed off the edge as a blitzer.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the defensive front, Andrew Van Ginkel, floated backward into coverage, and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers is actually the furthest outside blitzer.

With the all the down linemen sliding left, it provided Rodgers a free run into the backfield:

Watch again, and notice how the Packers tight end Josh Whyle — originally in motion —was ready for Rodgers and picked him up as he cut back toward the left side of Green Bay's line.

However, because his blocking assignment drew him in that direction, he wasn't positioned to help the right side of the Packers front that suddenly featured a right tackle stretched exceptionally wide by Murphy's cornerback blitz and Minnesota's most purely gifted outside rusher Dallas Turner erupting past the right guard.

Even when an offensive line thinks it picks up the blitzer Flores intended to get a free run, there's often a secondary hole opened for another defender to disrupt the pocket.

Flores absolutely will show all-out, eight-man pressure in this game. It's one of his trademarks. That doesn't always mean eight defenders are entering the rush on that play. In fact, that rarely happens. Discerning which defender(s) will drop into coverage is the challenge, particularly as the game clock is winding down.

Like here, against the Packers, the Vikings showed an eight-pass pressure package. Behind that hyper-aggressive look was plenty of green grass before three defensive backs roughly 10 yards beyond the line of scrimmage, splitting the field into thirds.

Pay close attention to what transpired at the snap and a split second later. The two outer most rushers on the left side of their defensive front show blitz but never actually rushed the quarterback, and linebacker Blake Cashman dropped into coverage underneath. On the edge, Van Ginkel watched the quarterback and kept contain.

Jordan Love missed a wide-open out-breaking route at the 40 yard line because he's forced into a quick decision which ultimately was a deep-ball attempt toward Christian Watson that was nearly intercepted.

The takeaway from that blitz is critical. Quite naturally, the Vikings have to drop at least one defender toward the side of the field with more receivers.

That feature of Minnesota's blitzes is noteworthy. It's the one distinct way an offense's pass game can dictate to the Vikings defense.

Note here, on this blitz against the Buccaneers, how linebacker Eric Wilson sunk at the snap toward the side of the field with three receivers for Tampa Bay.

And, sometimes, the sinking defender (occasionally it's two defenders) take three or four steps to sell blitz before retreating into a short zone.

There are two receivers to Jared Goff's right in this pre-snap alignment. At the snap, and even a second after it, the Vikings made a convincing case for an an all-out, eight-man pressure. But the blitz only featured seven, as Cashman exploded forward, disappeared into the middle of Detroit's offensive line then dropped into the middle of the field to take away Jahmyr Gibbs' underneath route.

In those all-out blitz looks, even if the Vikings ultimately send six or seven rushers — which is still an extremely high amount of rushers toward the quarterback — it's beneficial for the offense to feature as many routes with quick breaks off the vertical stem as possible.

On that specific play, notice how Jameson Williams and Amon Ra-St. Brown ran vertically and didn't have their heads fully turned around as Goff was being sacked.

Sure, the Lions were in a seven-man protection, but the offense can't assume every blocker will find his exact assignment in a flash after the snap.

And I've saved the most creative Flores blitz for last.

This came on a sack of Daniel Jones against the Colts.

Rather unusually, the Vikings were clearly in man coverage across the board — they've used man just 7.2% of the time, the lowest rate in the league and well below the NFL average of 22.4%. And it wasn't an all-out pressure look, as it was reasonably easy to discern Minnesota's five "known rushers" before the snap.

But pay close attention to the defender second-furthest from the left edge along Minnesota's front. It's Cashman, and at the snap, he started toward the Colts right tackle, as if he was going to deploy a stunt with edge rusher Dallas Turner. After selling the DT-DE stunt — Cash was effectively a defensive tackle on that play — he planted his foot in the ground to change directions completely and loop all the way through the A gap.

Unsurprisingly Cashman got a free run at Jones and registered the sack.

I don't believe I've ever seen that type of blitz before. That's not to say it's the first of its kind in NFL history, yet that type of creativity with one defender is exceptionally rare.

Imagine an entire offensive line group, extra blocking help in the backfield, and the quarterback processing everything in front of them in roughly 10-15 seconds after breaking the huddle and then again in one second after the snap.

It's precisely what makes facing this Flores defense so difficult.

Offenses know they're going to blitz on almost every snap.

But the Vikings don't care if they're predictable because they have such a wide variety of blitzes to stress the offensive communication throughout the duration of each contest.

#2777. Silva and Karetsas ensure Dortmund defeat Real Betis as Guirassy limps off

Borussia Dortmund held out for a slender 2-1 victory over Champions League opponents Real Betis tonight. Despite losing Serhou Guirassy to an early injury, goals from Fábio Silva and Kostas Karetsas sufficiently outgunned their visitors from the Andalusian capital.

The hosts probably should have taken the lead with a pair of chances inside eight minutes. Twice, Serhou Guirassy failed to steer home right flank deliveries from Julian Ryerson and Jobe Bellingham. Barring an offside goal for Betis star Antony, BVB were largely on top.

Following a couple sighters from Felix Nmecha outside the box, Alvaro Vallés produced a point-blank save to keep Daniel Svensson out. Betis also appeared in the final third at the other end, notably Abdessamad Ezzalzouli testing Gregor Kobel with a curling strike.

Dortmund were dealt a blow after the half-hour when Guirassy left the field with a suspected injury. On came Kostas Karetsas in his place, but the half would end without any noteworthy moments as both Natan and Ramy Bensebaini picked up bookings for fouls.

Having knocked away on the door for most of the first-half, it took just 4 minutes for BVB to open the scoring after the break. Ryerson put a low cross into the box for Bellingham to strike. The rebound off Vallés fell nicely to Silva, thrashing in from six yards out.

It could have gotten better soon after as Karetsas failed to beat Vallés. For all the hosts' dominance, Betis grabbed a lifeline through substitute Aitor Ruibal. A costly Anton mistake surrendered the ball, enabling Ezzalzouli to find the winger at the back post who converted.

Parity existed for the guts of 5 minutes in the end. Having just pulled off another fine parry to keep our Bellingham, Vallés failed to stop Karetsas deceiving his reach with a low drive. Niko Kovač quickly looked for fresh legs in Maxi Beier and Carney Chukwuemeka.

The Westphalians had a nervous end to the night as Isco started to pull the strings off the bench. A handful of late corners fell to the club from Seville, including one that bounced right through the area. Ultimately, a vital win for BVB as their European fixtures swifty turn tricky.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2775. Illinois volleyball falls short in unranked matchup to UCLA

CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Illinois needs some momentum heading to the homestretch of the season.

It didn't get it on Thursday night at Huff Hall as UCLA dispatched the Illini in four sets.

Head coach Chris Tamas made a bold lineup change, entrusting sophomore Sophi Randall to the starting setter position. This comes after Randall has been splitting sets with senior Kenna Phelan, whose spark seems to have dimmed. Randall has looked strong in recent matchups, with an exciting slide connection with middle Ashlyn Philpot.

UCLA was a great matchup for the Illini at this point in the season, as both teams are strong and unranked. To add on, UCLA entered the night on a four-match losing streak. This wasn't necessarily a "must win," but the momentum would've been nice looking ahead to a tough schedule.

Illinois threw the first punch of the night, winning the first set 25-17. However, it only went down from there. The Illini block coverage diminished in the second set, and the front row went silent. A glimmer of hope for the Illini Thursday was no doubt sophomore outside Alyssa Aguayo.

After a rough second and third set — Illinois dropped both, 25-15, 25-21 — Aguayo stood out in a struggling Illini lineup. Aguayo led the team with a whopping 19 kills, setting her career high. A strength of Aguayo's is her ability to slow the game down, and play technically. She is a player that is beautiful to watch, and holds herself in a composed manner. Head coach Chris Tamas agrees too.

"She's very steady and someone we rely on a lot," Tamas said. "We're gonna continue to rely on her as the season goes on."

The fourth set was a change in momentum for the Illini, senior Kenna Phelan entered the game in hopes to bring some defensive stability to the team. The change was definitely much needed, and lit a fire underneath her squad. The set was back-and-forth, with the Illini pushing the Bruins to a tie at 24-24. A serving error by Paityn Chapman returned UCLA the rock, and the game was ended by a blocked dump-set from Phelan.

That same story got told a lot Thursday night as the Illini managed to rack up 13 serving errors, led by freshman phenom Maya Harris with 4, and closely followed by Randall, who chipped in 3. The serving errors mixed with 23 attack errors, led to a flat outing.

The Illini now travel to face No. 22 Indiana, and undefeated No. 1 Nebraska, then meet No. 11 Penn State at Huff Hall. After this gauntlet of games, the Illini only have one opportunity to catch a breath of fresh air (unranked Iowa on Nov. 17) before heading to the first Big Ten Volleyball Tournament.

#2774. Three reasons the Jaguars beat the Ravens

The Jacksonville Jaguars continued their impressive 2026 campaign on Thursday night, dismantling the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 at M&T Bank Stadium. In a game played through torrential rain, Trevor Lawrence and the offense did enough to put points on the board, but it was another outstanding defensive performance that ultimately made the difference.

Jacksonville improved to 6-2, extending its lead at the top of the AFC South, while Baltimore suffered a fourth consecutive defeat. There were plenty of reasons for optimism in another convincing Jaguars victory, but these three stood out.

Jacksonville's defense has quietly become one of the most reliable units in the NFL, and Thursday night provided another demonstration of just how good this group can be.

The Jaguars entered Week 9 ranked second in the NFL in points allowed, and they backed that reputation up by limiting Baltimore to just 227 total yards, 10 first downs and 10 points. The Ravens converted just four of their 14 third-down opportunities, while Jacksonville forced three turnovers, including interceptions by Montaric Brown and Jourdan Lewis.

Brown's interception came on Baltimore's opening possession of the second half, immediately putting the Jaguars in position to extend their lead. Lewis provided another takeaway in the fourth quarter, with both interceptions ultimately helping Jacksonville add field goals.

There was also an important battle in the trenches. Despite losing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the season earlier in the week, Jacksonville restricted Derrick Henry to just 57 yards on 17 carries. That's an average of 3.4 yards per attempt against one of the most productive running backs of his generation.

Admittedly, Justice Hill's 65-yard touchdown run late in the fourth quarter took some of the shine off the final defensive numbers. However, until that point, Baltimore had managed just three points on its opening drive before going scoreless across its next nine offensive possessions.

The Ravens were missing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, but that shouldn't detract from the execution. Jacksonville did exactly what a good defense should do against a struggling offense: create pressure, take the football away and prevent the opposition from building any momentum.

This was another performance that suggests the Jaguars' defense can be a genuine strength as the season progresses.

Trevor Lawrence didn't need to put together a spectacular statistical performance to make his mark on this game. Instead, he delivered when Jacksonville needed him most.

The quarterback completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown, finishing with a 105.0 passer rating and spreading the football around eight different receivers.

His most important contribution came just before halftime. With the Jaguars holding a narrow 10-3 advantage, Lawrence led a four-play, 80-yard scoring drive that completely changed the complexion of the contest. The highlight was a beautifully executed 50-yard touchdown connection with Parker Washington, who beat his defender and found plenty of space behind the Baltimore secondary.

It was a significant moment. Jacksonville went into the locker room with a 17-3 lead rather than allowing the Ravens an opportunity to remain within one score and potentially build some momentum after the break.

Lawrence was particularly effective attacking downfield. According to Next Gen Stats, he completed eight of 10 passes travelling at least 10 air yards, accumulating 193 yards and a touchdown on those attempts. His 80% completion rate on downfield throws was his second-best mark of the season.

That's an encouraging development for a quarterback who has increasingly looked comfortable leading this offense.

There was no need for Lawrence to chase huge numbers in the second half. Jacksonville had established control, and he managed the game effectively while allowing the defense and special teams to do their jobs.

The Jaguars are becoming increasingly difficult to beat when their quarterback can produce big plays without needing to force the issue.

Perhaps the most encouraging aspect of this victory was how effectively Jacksonville's different units worked together.

This wasn't a game in which Lawrence needed to throw for 350 yards or the defense needed to score a touchdown to rescue the offense. Instead, the Jaguars consistently put themselves in advantageous positions and took the opportunities presented to them.

Their opening drive was an excellent example. Lawrence connected with tight end Nate Boerkircher for a 52-yard gain on the second play from scrimmage, setting up Bhayshul Tuten's one-yard touchdown run to give Jacksonville an early advantage.

The offense continued to find ways to move the football, while Cam Little converted all four of his field-goal attempts. Jacksonville finished with 319 total yards, averaging 5.7 yards per play, and produced seven scoring drives.

Importantly, the defense repeatedly helped the offense maintain control. Brown's interception set up a field goal early in the second half, while Lewis' fourth-quarter pick provided another short field. A fumble recovery by linebacker Jalen McLeod following the ensuing kickoff also helped Jacksonville put the game beyond doubt, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. eventually powering in from two yards out to make it 33-3.

It was a thoroughly professional performance in difficult conditions. The rain made life challenging for both offenses, but Jacksonville avoided the costly mistakes that could have allowed Baltimore back into the contest.

The Jaguars didn't need to dominate one particular statistical category to win. They simply executed their assignments, capitalized on mistakes and made sure the Ravens had very few opportunities to change the game's direction.

That's the kind of football that wins games in November and December.

There will be tougher tests ahead, and Jacksonville will need to maintain this level of performance against healthier and more dangerous opponents. However, back-to-back victories over the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens have provided plenty of evidence that this team deserves to be taken seriously.

Lawrence is playing some of the best football of his career, the defense is consistently producing results, and the supporting cast is doing its part.

At 6-2, the Jaguars are building a significant cushion in the AFC South. More importantly, they're beginning to look like a team capable of making some serious noise when the postseason arrives.

#2770. 5 things to watch as Giants face Eagles in Week 9 of 2026 NFL season

The Giants haven't won in Philadelphia since 2013, but this could be their big chance as the Eagles are having a rough year. They are 2-6 and reeling after quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the rest of the season due to blood clots. On Sunday, they'll be looking to avoid a seventh straight loss.

Let's review the top storylines to watch as the Giants continue their quest for the NFC East crown...

With Hurts out, the Giants probably expected to face Tanner McKee, a player who beat them in the 2024 season finale when he passed for 269 yards and two scores.

McKee was the subject of trade buzz during the offseason, with the suggestion being that some teams were looking at him as a potential starter. However, once he got his shot with the Eagles, he underwhelmed, losing three starts in a row and failing to exceed 215 passing yards in any of them.

Philadelphia has opted to make a change and give Milton a shot after acquiring the strong-armed former Patriots and Cowboys passer a few weeks ago. Although he has never started a game, Milton passed for 241 yards off the bench in last year's season finale with New England, so the Giants at least have some pro film of him to get a sense of what he brings to the table.

New York's running backs came up big in their last game, the overtime win against the Texans in Houston. Four different players rushed for a touchdown, including Devin Singletary's walk-off game winner. However, as rumors of potential interest in a trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor circulate, the running game situation is unclear.

The Giants recently released Najee Harris and may wish they hadn't, because Tyrone Tracy Jr. has since landed on IR. In addition, Cam Skattebo, who rushed for over 100 yards against the Texans, is dealing with a hamstring issue and could be a game-time decision. This would leave Singletary under pressure to deliver, with some inexperienced players behind him on the bench.

Considered by many a long-shot to even make the roster this season, Banks is finally living up to his draft position.

Banks, who won an NFL Defensive Player of the Week Award last month, furthered his renewed reputation in the Texans game by impressively holding Nico Collins to just two catches for six yards.

Oct 4, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks (2) reacts after breaking up a pass intended for Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride (85) during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. / Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images

New York just signed Greg Newsome II to a three-year extension, and Banks reportedly rejected a similar deal at the same time. He will no doubt want to prove he's worth more than Newsome and should have a good chance to do that.

With A.J. Brown now in New England and DeVonta Smith nursing a hamstring injury, rookie Makai Lemon leads the Eagles with 31 receptions, but he's only averaging 8.1 yards per catch.

One area where the Jets might have the edge is in the kicking game, because the usually stellar Harrison Butker has really been struggling. #2766. 4 keys to a Jets win vs. the Chiefs in Week 9

The New York Jets don't have much room for error as they enter Week 9. At 2-6, another defeat would extend a frustrating stretch and make a return to relevance nearly impossible. The challenge is substantial. Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes have built a track record of making opponents pay for even the smallest mistakes.

The Kansas City Chiefs enter Week 9 at 5-2, but consecutive losses have shown some vulnerability. That doesn't mean they are suddenly an easy opponent, especially at Arrowhead Stadium. The Jets will need to play with discipline, maintain control of the game's tempo, and take advantage of their opportunities.

New York has shown flashes of being competitive, but turning those moments into a complete performance is another matter. These four things will be especially important to ensure a victory on Sunday.

The Jets won the time-of-possession battle against the Las Vegas Raiders, but barely. New York held the ball for 30:02 compared with 29:58 for the Raiders. Las Vegas also had three scoring drives that lasted at least five minutes, while the Jets had only two. That won't be good enough against Mahomes.

One of the best ways to challenge Reid's offense is to keep it on the sideline. Longer possessions would give Glenn's defense more time to recover while putting additional pressure on the Kansas City defense to stay on the field.

Dylan Laube's second-quarter kickoff return for a touchdown changed the complexion of Sunday's game. Without that breakdown, the Jets could have carried a much larger advantage into halftime.

There's no way to know how the rest of the game would have unfolded, but surrendering seven points without the defense having an opportunity to make a stop is difficult to overcome, maybe. One can never tell. Maybe

New York has allowed too many momentum-changing special teams plays. Against Mahomes on the road, giving away a touchdown is a luxury the Jets simply cannot afford.

The Jets cannot afford to abandon the running game if the offense doesn't find immediate success. That becomes particularly important against a Kansas City defense allowing just 96.3 rushing yards per game, with only seven other teams surrendering fewer entering Week 9.

Staying competitive on the scoreboard will allow New York to remain patient and maintain some balance. Falling behind by multiple scores would make that considerably harder, putting too much responsibility on Smith and the passing game.

Geno Smith and Braelon Allen need to carry their Week 8 production into this matchup. Allen is coming off a 147-yard performance, a big boost for an offense that finally showed some explosiveness.

However, moving the ball between the 20-yard lines won't be enough. The Jets enter Week 9 ranked last in the NFL in red-zone touchdown percentage at 42.3%, and they converted just two of six opportunities against Las Vegas. Field goals won't consistently keep pace with Kansas City. New York needs touchdowns.

Kansas City is built to punish opponents who let the game get away from them. The Jets need to make this a game of patience and execution rather than one dictated by Mahomes and the Chiefs' offensive firepower. New York has spent too many Sundays watching opportunities slip away. This time, it must make the most of every chance before the final minutes arrive.

#2761. Clay Travis pushes back on Curt Cignetti’s claim ESPN favors the SEC

Curt Cignetti's accusation that ESPN's college football voices push the SEC drew a response Thursday from Clay Travis, the OutKick founder who now works as a Fox News contributor and hosts a weekly show on FS1. The Indiana Hoosiers coach made his case on his weekly radio show Wednesday, one day after the College Football Playoff selection committee released its first rankings of the season.

That first top 25 included 10 SEC teams and six from the Big Ten. Indiana debuted at No. 4 at 8-1, one spot ahead of a two-loss Alabama Crimson Tide team, while a 6-2 Iowa Hawkeyes team sat at No. 19.

"We Will Never See This Again": Analyst Stunned By Curt Cignetti's Historic Run After Hoosier's Big Ten Championship Image Via Instagram/@elitecollegefootball)

"Come on. These people, and there's a whole bunch of them, they march out of the tent, and they're given instructions on what to say, they follow the company line. Right, and I don't need to go any further. SEC gets a lot of love from the ESPN, you know, and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum. So that's why you see all these SEC teams up there, you know, and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten, not quite as high. But like I said, it's all going to be played out on the field," Cignetti said.

ESPN holds the SEC's national television rights and the rights to the College Football Playoff, and it aired Tuesday's rankings reveal. The rankings themselves come from the selection committee, so Cignetti's complaint is aimed at the noise around that room more than the room itself.

"Curt Cignetti says ESPN is biased toward the SEC. I disagree. In my entire media career, nobody has ever told me what I can or cannot do. Maybe the reason the SEC has so many teams ranked highly is because it's actually the best conference in college football," Travis wrote on X.

Travis answered a charge about ESPN with his own career, and he has never worked for ESPN. He has spent more than a decade at Fox, the Big Ten's lead television partner, and has been one of ESPN's most persistent critics for most of that time.

In October 2025, Travis reported on OutKick that ESPN had pulled Paul Finebaum from its programming after Finebaum discussed a possible U.S. Senate run in an interview with him. ESPN spokesman Bill Hofheimer publicly denied the report. Travis was alleging then the same kind of network control over ESPN talent that he is waving off now that Cignetti is the one alleging it.

Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti coaches his team against Ohio State Buckeyes in the third quarter during the football game in Columbus on Saturday, Nov. 23, 2024.

Ten SEC teams in the committee's top 25 is the best evidence for Travis' side of the conference argument, and the committee, not a network, put them there. At the top of the sport, the Big Ten owns the last three national championships through Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana. Cignetti's Hoosiers finished 16-0 last season and beat Alabama 38-3 in the Rose Bowl quarterfinal on the way, and no SEC team has played in the national title game since Georgia won it after the 2022 season.

Cignetti closed his remarks by saying it will all be played out on the field. For three straight Januarys, the field has sided with the Big Ten.

#2759. Three reasons why the Brewers can repeat as World Series champions in 2027

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Milwaukee Brewers are the freshly crowned World Series champions for 2026. Add that trophy to a regular season body of work in which they won 103 games and achieved the best run differential in all of Major League Baseball, and it's clear the Brewers this season did all a team can do. The first title in franchise history will be remembered and cherished by the Brewers and their fans forever, and it was earned in every respect.

The celebrations won't soon end, and the post-Game 5 hangovers are still pulsing. Even so, it's time to turn our attention to the 2027 season and explore why the Brewers absolutely have the foundation necessary to do it all again next year. Here, then, are three reasons the Brewers can become repeat champions roughly one year from now.

Eyeball the Brewers' current contract obligations and service time tiers, and you'll find just six players are likely bound for free agency. Brandon Woodruff, Jake Bauers, JoJo Romero, and Gary Sánchez will be free agents soon. Elsewhere, Dustin May has a mutual option for 2027, which means he'll probably join them. Finally, Antonio Senzatela has a $14 million team option for 2027 on which the Brewers may pass.

Of those, the 31-year-old Bauers is the biggest needle-mover, as he's coming off a 2026 season in which he hit 26 home runs in 144 games and put up a WAR of 3.3. He does seem likely to move on, but the Brewers are more than resourceful enough to find comparable production from the non-premium position of first base.

Elsewhere, the Brewers should resist the temptation to trade away catcher, linchpin, and reigning World Series MVP William Contreras ahead of his walk year in 2027. The Brewers Way in recent years has been to part ways with core contributors around such a time, and that may be a temptation with Contreras, especially given Bo Naylor's presence on the roster. Contreras, though, is not easily replaceable given his skills behind the mask and his high level of production at the plate. An extension may not be something the Brewers will pursue – even though the ongoing CBA negotiations will probably lead to a new system that benefits teams like Milwaukee – but even if that's the case, they should keep their catcher and leader around for the final year of team control in the name of defending the belt and the title.

The champion Brewers, as a club that gets limited investment from ownership and is elite at player development, skews young even as they stand as the best team in baseball. Consider:

As for specific examples, they're not hard to find. Budding star Jackson Chourio will be in his age-23 campaign in 2027. Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson will each be 25. Cooper Pratt, like Chourio, will be 23. The Brewers this past season got 16.4 WAR from those names, and Pratt and Henderson didn't even log full seasons.

Let's also note that Brice Turang, who led the Brewers this season with a WAR of 7.3, will be just 27 in '27 and thus should continue performing at a high level. This isn't just a matter of the Brewers being largely shielded from age-related decline next season. There's also the distinct possibility that so many of their 2026 pace-setters are still pre-prime and may have even better days ahead.

As though all of the above weren't enough, the Brewers right now have managed to thread this rare needle: they're the best team at the highest level and have one of the best collections of talent down on the farm. MLB.com in August ranked the Brewers as the third-best farm system in the game right now. FanGraphs ranked them third based on average prospect value. Baseball America at midseason likewise ranked the Milwaukee system third and after the season gave the system an "A" grade.

At an individual level, a number of premium Brewers prospects figure to arrive at some point next season. That list includes shortstop Jesús Made, who may be the top prospect in the game right now. Other 2027 arrivals may include talents like corner infielder Andrew Fischer, right-handers Tyson Hardin and Bishop Letson, and infielder/outfielder Jett Williams, among others. So many teams in contending mode have a fairly dry pipeline thanks to the low draft picks and the now-for-later trades that often accompany World Series aspirations, but that's very much not the case with lead executive Matt Arnold and the Brewers.

Celebrations of the work done in 2026 should be the focus right now for the Crew and their rooters, and once that dies down, they can all be further buoyed by the reality that the Brewers aren't going anywhere. The guess here is that the Brewers open the 2027 season – whatever it looks like — as the consensus favorites to do it all again.

#2757. Brewers set World Series parade for Friday, two days after winning 2026 title

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

In keeping with the ancient laws of combat, the Milwaukee Brewers are hereby entitled to a parade. The Brewers, with their win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 on Wednesday night, secured the World Series title for 2026 – their first such title in franchise history – and soon it'll be time to celebrate the occasion.

Speaking of which, the City of Milwaukee on Thursday announced plans for the Brewers' championship parade, which will take place on Friday, Oct. 30. Here are the essentials:

What: Brewers Parade of Champions and Championship RallyWhere: Starting at N. 4th St. and W. Wisconsin Ave. in downtown Milwaukee and ending at Henry Maier Festival ParkWhen: Starting at 10 a.m. CST on Friday, Oct. 30Cost: The parade is free and open to the publicTV/streaming: Nationally on MLB Network, MLB.tv, Brewers.tv, and Brewers.com (fuboTV, try for free); locally on CBS 58 starting at 9 a.m. CST.

The rally at Henry Maier Festival Park opens at 8 a.m. and will include large video screens featuring live parade coverage, live music, food and beverage offerings, exclusive merchandise and more. Brewers alumni will also be in attendance and the first 50,000 fans at the rally will receive a limited-edition championship rally towel.

🏆 Milwaukee, the celebration continues!Join the @Brewers for the Parade of Champions tomorrow, Friday, Oct. 30! 💙💛Starts at 10 AM at N. 4th St. & W. Wisconsin Ave., ending at Summerfest grounds for the Championship Rally!Full details: https://t.co/0r5qC7R61X pic.twitter.com/9CQJmK9Vzz

Milwaukee Public Schools also announced that school will be canceled for all students and staff on Friday for the parade and celebration.

Given the enthusiasm shown by Brewers fans throughout this season and especially the playoffs – they may have been the majority presence in Game 5 at Tropicana Field – it no doubt will be an enthusiastic and memorable celebration. Brewers supporters, after all, have been waiting 57 years for just such an event.

#2756. Niko Kovač: Jobe Bellingham has “fully deserved” first England call-up

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham has received his first call-up to the England senior squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, BVB head coach Niko Kovač reflected on the 21-year-old's selection, which will give him the opportunity to represent England alongside his older brother, Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham.

"He has truly deserved it. The progress he has made has been tremendous. He has invested a lot of effort and works extremely hard. And the way he has gone about things this year has been excellent. You have to acknowledge that he needed a bit of time. Many people don't have the patience, but that's what he's shown," Kovač said.

"You can see that he is truly fantastic. I'm happy for him and delighted that he can now pull on the national team shirt alongside his brother. That's something special – not just representing your country, but doing so alongside your own brother as well. It's fantastic.

"He should keep going, and I'm convinced he will, because he has a tremendous attitude, loves what he does, and has everything it takes to become a truly great player."

Jobe Bellingham joined Borussia Dortmund from Sunderland in the summer of 2025. He has made 14 appearances for BVB this season, including 10 starts.

#2754. Top 25 MLB trade candidates for 2026-27 offseason: Paul Skenes, Jeremy Peña and more who could move

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With the Milwaukee Brewers crowned as the 2026 World Series champions, the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is now upon us.

While the arc, pace, and even length of this offseason are all uncertain thanks to the ongoing CBA negotiations, we do know that at some point before the next season begins, we'll have a flurry of free agent signings and trades. The focus in this space right now is on the latter: possible winter trades.

We're about to examine the 25 leading trade candidates of the offseason. Obviously, this won't be an exhaustive list of players who might be traded, and just as obviously not all of these names to come will be on the move. Some, though, will, and all of these names have been deemed as distinct possibilities based on reporting, service time and payroll considerations, and prior organizational decision-making.

We'll explore names by putting them in groups based on the underlying reasons or causes of their status as trade candidates. Here are those groups:

The 25 names to come won't be ranked, but instead will be listed alphabetically within their respective categories. Now let's get to it.

Duran's taken a serious fall from the heights of 2024, when he earned an All-Star selection and cracked the top 10 of the American League MVP vote. He cratered last season, which makes this winter something of an inopportune time to trade him from the Boston standpoint. That said, the Red Sox have a crowded outfield with Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Roman Anthony, which means a Duran swap may be needed to clear the decks. If nothing else, the 30-year-old outfielder presents a buy-low/change-of-scenery opportunity for a team looking to take a risk.

Potential fits: Phillies, Cubs, Mariners, Rangers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 50%

Hernández has been a reliable power presence for the Dodgers, but now, at age 34, he's been showing some signs of decline. On another level, the Dodgers want to make space for elite prospect Josue De Paula to receive regular playing time, and there aren't any other paths to it. That may mean Hernández will be on the move.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Kwan's another who's been a reliable presence in the trade rumors for some time. Cleveland also has a history of dealing core talents leading up to their walk year, and Kwan is indeed slated for free agency after next season. The timing would be right, as Kwan is coming off a 5.0-WAR season for the second time in his career.

Potential fits: Phillies, Blue Jays, Cubs, Mariners

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

McClanahan's long and labored comeback from Tommy John surgery was finally realized this past season, and he turned in a strong age-29 campaign for the Rays. These, though, are the Rays, and McClanahan's forthcoming arbitration payday combined with his uncertain health history may prompt them to shop him to pitching-starved fellow contenders. He carries risk, of course, but there will no doubt be potential takers lining up for him.

Potential fits: Braves, Padres, Orioles, Tigers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Thanks to a blazing fastball and wipeout knuckle curve, the soon-to-be 33-year-old Megill has been a lockdown closer for most of the last three seasons. The Brewers of course have a substantial history of trading away closers before they reach their high-salary years and also before they regress/decline (see: Hader, Josh and Williams, Devin). That could again be the case with Megill, who'll be in line for free agency after the 2027 season.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 55%

He's the most dominant closer in baseball and the owner of one of the biggest fastballs ever, and he's under team control through the 2029 season. So why would the contending Padres trade Miller at the peak of his powers? They'd consider doing so because they have a lot of roster holes to fill elsewhere, especially with Michael King opting out of his contract. Trading away Miller would in theory allow them to fill some of those holes, which is why it'll be a temptation for lead executive AJ Preller. No doubt, fellow contenders will be lining up if the Pads do indeed shop the NL saves leader.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

Strider not so long ago was in the discussion for most dominant starter in the bigs, but persistent arm woes have turned him into a question mark. The Braves came close to dealing Strider at the deadline in exchange for more of a known quantity in the rotation, so there's basis for his inclusion on this list. Any team acquiring him will have to be comfortable with Strider's medicals and the fact that he's owed a minimum of $49 million over the next two seasons. His ace upside, though, is surely tantalizing.

Potential fits: Cardinals, Padres, Orioles, Tigers, Dodgers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

The Nats were clear sellers at the deadline, but they retained Abrams, who has two full years of team control remaining. In other words, it's going to take a lot to pry him away. At 26, he's coming off a 30-30 season, and he's been a quite productive bat over the last three years. Defensively, Abrams probably isn't an everyday shortstop moving forward, but second base is now in his toolkit.

Potential fits: Braves, Pirates, Red Sox, Giants, Rangers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

Teams will pay a lot for a young and controllable starting pitcher with frontline upside, and all of that describes the 27-year-old lefty Detmers. Not eligible for free agency until after the 2028 season, Detmers topped 4.0 WAR this past season and struck out 211 batters in 185 innings. For the Halos, trading him might be an example of selling high.

Potential fits: Cardinals, Red Sox, Cubs, Blue Jays, Padres

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

As a 27-year-old All-Star catcher with three full seasons of team control remaining, Goodman would cost a lot in trade. Perhaps that's why the rebuilding Rockies will indeed deal him this winter. There's no doubt that playing his home games in Coors Field helps Goodman's cause, but this past season, he was actually much more productive on the road. Away from Coors, he hit 25 of his 41 home runs in 2026, and his road slugging percentage was .564 versus a .490 figure at a mile above sea level. That's power that will play anywhere.

Potential fits: Giants, White Sox, Yankees, Orioles

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 50%

Greene has one of the biggest fastballs in the game and a top 10 finish in the NL Cy Young balloting in his recent past. However, he's struggled to stay healthy and realize his potential on a sustained basis – the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2017. He's signed through 2028 with a club option for 2029, and it may be time for a change of scenery. He's been the subject of trade speculation before.

Potential fits: Dodgers, Braves, Red Sox, Astros, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

Herrera is not a particularly skilled defensive catcher outside of blocking pitches in the dirt, but he can get by behind the mask, at least on a part-time basis. He also has a plus bat, which will play at DH or perhaps first base and even left field. The Cardinals have an incoming glut of catchers, which means it may be time to move on from Herrera. He's not eligible for free agency until after the 2029 season.

Potential fits: Yankees, White Sox, Orioles, Giants

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

The Marlins seem likely to trade away one of their middle infielders this winter, either the shortstop Lopez or second baseman Xavier Edwards. For now, we'll focus on Lopez, who would likely fetch the higher return. The 28-year-old Lopez this past season topped 6.0 WAR, led the NL in hits, and swiped 34 bases, all while grading out as a valuable defender at the premium position of short. He's under team control through the 2029 season, which means he'll have immense trade value.

Potential fits: Braves, Phillies, Red Sox, Rays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

The most underrated player in baseball? The 25-year-old Neto is very much in that discussion. Over the last three seasons, he's amassed a WAR of 15.6, which puts him in elite territory. Any team in need of excellence and stability on the left side of the infield should have interest. Neto isn't eligible for free agency until after the 2029 season, which adds to his already substantial trade value.

Potential fits: Braves, Red Sox, Tigers, Cardinals, Yankees

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

No, this one isn't likely to happen, as Contreras has proved central to the Brewers' success in 2026 and for years prior. That said, the ever-resourceful Brewers do have a ready replacement on the roster in Bo Naylor. The 2026 World Series MVP is also in line for free agency after the 2027 season, which theoretically increases the chances that Milwaukee will explore his trade market. Speaking of which, such a skilled catcher with a potent bat and reputation as a leader will indeed have a healthy market.

Potential fits: Yankees, Rangers, Orioles

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

For years now, it seems, we've been waiting for the Mariners to trade from their surfeit of starting pitching. They moved Luis Castillo at the deadline, but perhaps this time, they finally flip one of their big guns. Gilbert, 29, will be a pending free agent in 2027, which straightaway makes him a trade candidate for a Mariners club that's more averse to spending than they should be. He's an attractive one, too, as Gilbert has been a reliable source of innings over his career to date, and he also boasts a 3.58 FIP and a sparkling 5.14 K/BB ratio over the last four seasons.

Potential fits: Mets, Braves, Orioles, Cubs, White Sox

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Paredes, who turns 28 in February, is on a $13.35 million team option for 2027, and then he's eligible for free agency. That adds up to the real possibility of a trade out of Houston. While there are questions as to how Paredes' bat will play without the Crawford Boxes near at hand, there's no doubt he's overall a valuable performer. He's fresh off a 4.0-WAR season in 2026 and relatively young as notable trade targets go.

Potential fits: Phillies, Cardinals, Yankees

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Peña, like Paredes, will be a pending free agent in 2027, and the increasingly incompetent Astros may look to trade him as they did Kyle Tucker back in the winter of 2024-25. Peña, 29, hasn't been especially durable over the last two seasons, but when on the field, he remains an excellent all-around performer. If he is indeed shopped, then he's the most appealing shortstop on the trade and free agent markets this offseason.

Potential fits: Braves, Red Sox, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Ryan has been the subject of trade speculation for what feels like the last half-decade. Has the time finally come for those rumors to be realized? Now 30, Ryan will be a free agent after the 2027 season, and that of course means he could be on the move this winter. He has excellent stuff, and over the last three seasons Ryan boasts an ERA+ of 117 and a K/BB ratio of 5.38.

Potential fits: Cubs, Astros, Mets, Orioles, Red Sox, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Yes, deGrom is 38, but going into the final guaranteed year of his contract, he remains capable of being a solid rotation presence for a contender. deGrom reportedly used his full no-trade clause to block a trade to the Braves at the deadline, so it's far from certain whether he'd be willing to approve a deal out of Arlington. That said, such things are always negotiations, and a late-career run at the playoffs might prove tempting for him.

Potential fits: Braves, Dodgers, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

The future Hall of Famer is coming off another solid season once you consider that a spring hamate injury likely sapped his production early on. That said, he soon turns 33, and he's still owed $160 million through 2031. That's in addition to his full no-trade clause. The Mets and Lindor, though, may be at a crossroads in their relationship, which makes it at least theoretically possible that a change of scenery is in the offing.

Potential fits: Braves, Mariners, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

Marte already had a partial no-trade clause in his contract, which runs through 2030 (with a 2031 player option), and now he's earned a full no-trade clause through 10-and-5 rights. That said, after multiple somewhat bizarre AWOL incidents with the D-backs, Marte and the club may be looking for a fresh start. While Marte's offensive outputs dipped last season, his age-32 campaign, he still profiles as at least an above-average player for the near- to mid-term. And he may be more than that if he gets back to something like his pre-2026 peak.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

Now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. With the Rangers perhaps looking to shed payroll, they could seek to move Seager, who's owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. As with the Mets and Lindor, that may mean kicking in cash to make a trade happen, but Seager would help the cause for any contender in need of help at the shortstop position.

Potential fits: Braves, Mariners, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

Will the increasingly listless Reds pivot toward a longer-term rebuild? If they do, then their electric 24-year-old shortstop could be dangled. De La Cruz is coming off his best season to date, and there's the feeling that he still has offensive upside in the tank. He's under team control through the 2029 season. Those three full years of control plus De La Cruz's MVP upside mean we'd be talking about a true blockbuster of a trade. No, it's not particularly likely to happen, but it's an intriguing possibility.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

This is becoming something of an annual exercise in speculation and wish-casting (wish-casting by non-Pirates fans, anyway). Skenes took a step back last season in terms of run prevention and underlying indicators, and he also lost a bit off his fastball. Still, he was overall a high-value pitcher who still projects as an ace, and he's not far removed from those legendary rookie and sophomore seasons. Like De La Cruz above, Skenes has three more full seasons before free agency, which makes his trade value pretty well stratospheric. The Pirates aren't likely at all to move him, particularly ahead of a new CBA that may benefit teams of their sort, but the Skenes trade conjecture isn't going anywhere.

#2753. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2751. Demichelis insists Leipzig deserved more after Manchester City defeat

RB Leipzig head coach Martín Demichelis believes his side deserved more than a point following Wednesday's 3-2 Champions League defeat to Manchester City.

Despite producing an impressive display against the 2023 European champions, the Red Bulls were left empty-handed as Erling Haaland netted his 13th goal in nine outings against them.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, former City defender Demichelis expressed his frustration at the result, but was full of praise for his players.

“That's football. I think, in my personal opinion, we deserved more than a point today,” the Argentine said.

"We produced an outstanding performance today against the team currently second in the Premier League, a team that will probably fight for titles until the very end.

“I believe today we produced our best performance without the ball, and we were also brave going forward with the ball, creating plenty of chances."

Looking back at how Leipzig lost, Demichelis was particularly frustrated by the way his side conceded.

“Look we conceded the first goal, which we scored ourselves,” he said, recalling Castello Lukeba's first-half own goal.

"At that moment, I don't think Manchester City had even a shot on goal.

“On the other hand, Haaland wasn't involved in the game, and in the end he scores the third goal. That's football.”

As a result of the defeat, Leipzig are left with just three points from their opening four outings on their return to European football. Still, Demichelis believes that the performance demonstrated that his side can compete at a very high level.

"I know that three points from four games isn't enough. But the way we played today, that's exactly what this team needs to show in every game.

"It was very bitter. It's a very sad moment for the players, but I simply congratulated the players. That's the way forward.

“And that's the kind of performance we need to show in this international competition. Today was a proper Champions League game.”

With the Red Bulls still harbouring hopes of reaching the playoffs, Demichelis urged his squad to “take confidence from a performance like that”, adding that Leipzig “always keep going.”

For now, attention turns to Augsburg on Saturday, before Leipzig have the chance to bounce back against RC Lens in Europe at the end of the month.

#2747. Yankees staring at sweep after ALDS Game 2 loss to Rays; Falcons run roughshod over Saints on 'MNF'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

Don't look now, but Bob Chesney has UCLA ranked inside the top 25 just four games into his tenure. In fact, the Bruins are ranked even higher than that in Brandon Marcello's latest CFB Power Rankings.

UCLA had an open date last week as it geared up for a top-25 game against Oregon this weekend, but it still climbed into the top 10 of our rankings. Not only does Chesney have the Bruins offense humming, but he also has the chance to get a little revenge after leading James Madison against the Ducks in last year's College Football Playoff.

Here's a little snippet of the complete rankings:

21. Virginia Tech (-1) 22. Houston (NR) 23. Iowa (-7) 24. Mississippi State (-13) 25. USC (-2)

One team that's pretty far away from any top 10 ranking these days is Penn State, which is coming off a humiliating loss to Northwestern. The Nittany Lions plummeted 12 spots in the latest edition of the CBS Sports 138, and they're barely hanging on inside the top 50.

Oh, and to make matters worse, Penn State is one of the 10 teams that landed on our Panic Meter after Week 5.

It won't be long before the 2026-27 NBA season tips off, and our team of experts is here to get you ready. Today, our own John Gonzalez is ranking the best starting fives from around the league.

In that regard, it's hard to beat the defending champion Knicks. Their quintet of oft-doubted stars returns after rolling to a title in last year's postseason. That said, they have serious competition within their own division.

The 76ers had quite the offseason, and their starting five looks a lot more formidable with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in the mix. President of basketball operations Mike Gansey deserves a lot of credit for his summer masterclass.

Besides, the Knicks are currently in a contentious contract negotiation with a member of their starting five. According to Karl-Anthony Towns, extension talks "don't look good" with the season right around the corner. We've already seen one sour negotiation end on a positive note, so maybe Towns and New York can find a resolution.
